nodes.label: Account Aggregation
nodes.rationale: Aggregates held-away assets into consolidated net worth. nodes.label: Attack Surface: Aggregation Reliability
nodes.rationale: CONFIRMED across three independent review sites (G2, Capterra, Software Advice, 2026). Connections break, clients re-authenticate repeatedly, credit unions poorly covered. Reviewer language: 'very brittle', 'constant connection issues… to the point of making the software useless'. Aggregation is unsolved even for the market leader — a differentiation opportunity AND the hardest subsystem to build. Caveat: learning-curve and price complaints recur at least as often; this is merely the most concrete TECHNICAL complaint.

nodes.label: Attack Surface: Learning Curve & Silent Modeling Errors
nodes.rationale: CONFIRMED (high confidence). Kitces: 3–6 months to advisor proficiency on the cash-flow engine. Documented G2 case: a non-intuitive Social Security setting silently stacked early-claiming reductions on statement-entered amounts, understating an age-63 benefit until the CLIENT challenged the numbers. Even 5-star fans call the interface 'kind of clunky'. This is where RightCapital and MoneyGuidePro win — ease and speed-to-plan, not raw modeling power. Design implication: build assumption-input guardrails/validation from day one.

nodes.label: No Estate / Inheritance / Gift Tax in T&T
nodes.rationale: CONFIRMED (high confidence). No inheritance, estate, or gift taxes in T&T. US-style estate-tax modeling is largely INAPPLICABLE — shifts estate features toward asset TITLING, SUCCESSION, and PROBATE (Succession Act Ch. 9:02), with an optional stamp-duty calculator for gifts/conveyances. NeedsEngine correctly OMITS the US estate-tax liquidity driver, and golden-file tests assert no estate-tax driver.

nodes.label: 25% Approved-Annuity Early Surrender Tax
nodes.rationale: CONFIRMED (high confidence). Early surrender of a BIR-approved annuity: 25% tax on the withdrawn amount, only premiums refunded (gains forfeited), BIR approval required for surrender. Analogous to but structurally different from the US 10% penalty. Only BIR-approved annuities qualify for the pension/annuity deduction — model approved vs non-approved as DISTINCT ACCOUNT TYPES.

nodes.label: T&T Aggregation Infeasibility
nodes.rationale: ⚠️ UNRESOLVED in this report — 'the biggest open question' and 'the single largest technical-feasibility question for the product'. NO CLAIMS survived to verification. Open Banking Tracker catalogs 43 T&T institutions with NO confirmed developer portals for any T&T bank. Early signals suggest no native open-banking APIs exist, making direct integrations, screen-scraping partnerships, or well-designed manual/statement-import the realistic paths. RESOLVED LATER by the spec: Round 2 confirmed no aggregator (Plaid, Salt Edge) covers a single Caribbean bank — but an insurance-first product's data source is POLICY DOCUMENTS, not bank APIs, so the blocker mostly dissolves. Bank aggregation is explicitly out of scope.

nodes.label: The NIS ⊕ SCP Interaction (clawback)
nodes.rationale: ✅ CONFIRMED FROM PRIMARY SOURCE (scraped from the Ministry's own page and application form, social.gov.tt) — gate lifted. Senior Citizens' Pension is MEANS-TESTED against assessed monthly income: ≤2,500→3,500 · 2,501–3,500→2,500 · 3,501–4,500→1,500 · 4,501–5,500→500 · >5,500→NIL (hard disqualification). Age 65+, residency 20 yrs preceding (absences ≤5) OR 50 yrs aggregate. NIS RETIREMENT PENSION COUNTS AS ASSESSED INCOME (application form item 6 'Evidence of National Insurance Benefits' and item 31 'how much is your monthly pension?'); the ONE-TIME GRANT IS EXCLUDED. THE MODAL OUTCOME: no NIS → SCP 3,500 → total 3,500. NIS minimum 3,000 → SCP 2,500 → total 5,500. A TTD 3,000 NIS PENSION DELIVERS ONLY 2,000 — an effective ~33% clawback at the minimum-pension level. NOT AN EDGE CASE: THE COMMON CASE. COUNTER-INTUITIVE AND TRUE: SCP's maximum (3,500) EXCEEDS the NIS minimum pension (3,000) — worth stating plainly in client-facing output. CONSEQUENCES: (1) NeedsEngine MUST model NIS and SCP together — modeling NIS alone materially OVERSTATES the value of NIS contributions and UNDERSTATES the retirement gap; this is A CORRECTNESS FIX, NOT AN ENHANCEMENT. (2) HARD CLIFF EDGES at 2,500/3,500/4,500/5,500 — at 5,501 one extra dollar costs 500/month; the engine must REFUSE to land a client just over a cliff without flagging it. (3) 'Precisely the class of local complexity that makes the engine uncopyable — no US tool has any analogue.' 🔴 A prior verification round REFUTED these exact bands 1–2 and declared the interaction unverifiable, causing the spec to downgrade a correct insight to 'fiction'. Both that and the NIBTT fabrication OVERRODE THE PRACTITIONER AND WERE WRONG; both answers sat on the issuing agency's own website.

nodes.label: T-T-Financial-Insurance-Hub Repo
nodes.author: Kelsean868
nodes.rationale: 'A substantial chunk of ParameterTables already written.' Five calculators, 100% HTML on GitHub Pages, SEO'd, public — THE HTML IS A PROTOTYPE; THE LOGIC IS THE ASSET. Constants: PERSONAL_ALLOWANCE 90,000/yr; TAX_BRACKET_1_LIMIT 1,000,000; TAX_RATE_1 0.25, TAX_RATE_2 0.30; MAX_DEDUCTIBLE_NIS_ANNUITY_COMBINED 60,000 (✅ independently CONFIRMS Round 1's panel, which killed the government's stale TT$30,000 figure 0–3 — two independent sources now agree); 70% of NIS contributions deductible (NEW — we had no such rule, and ⚪ ENTIRELY UNVERIFIED per the July 2026 audit); Health Surcharge 4.80/wk if monthly ≤469.99 else 8.25/wk (a deduction ABSENT from our spec entirely); PENSION_CONTRIB_THRESHOLD 750 weeks ✅; MIN_NIS_PENSION 3000 ✅; MIN_NIS_GRANT 3000; 16 earnings classes each with basicMonthly + incrementMonthly; pension = basicMonthly + floor(excessContributions/25) × incrementMonthly; grant = totalMonetaryValue × 3. 'Our spec said 16-class banded system ABSTRACTLY. THIS IS THE ACTUAL FORMULA.' Also present: Section 134(6) corporate annuity logic, public servants' pension + gratuity (a separate regime covering a large share of T&T employment — another gap in our spec), and a 2019–2024 tax return calculator. ⚠️ THE DATA IS TEN YEARS STALE — most recent embedded table is 2016-09-05; the 16.2%/2026 and 19.2%/2027 rates and the 2028 retirement-age phase-up are NONE OF THEM IN THE REPO. 'The architecture is right; the data has drifted' — the strongest possible argument for parameter discipline, since the tables went stale in exactly the way we predicted, IN CODE WRITTEN BY SOMEONE WHO KNEW TO DATE THEM. Per the spec, BOTH halves are architecturally correct: getTableForDate() era-selects contributions ✅ and PENSION_RATES is a single claim-date table ✅ — the only defect is MISSING PROVENANCE (add 'effective 2008-01-07' + source URL). Distribution asset: five public SEO'd calculators already live and indexed — someone computing their take-home pay or NIS pension is self-identifying as exactly the person who needs a needs analysis (idea #9, public value + lead-gen, already built).

nodes.label: Year-Indexed Dated Parameter Tables
nodes.source_location: The repo already implements our hardest rule
nodes.rationale: The repo embeds 13 DATED contribution-rate tables spanning 1972 → 2016 — that IS the 'no bare constants, always year-indexed and dated' discipline the spec demands, already built in production by the same author. THREE INDEPENDENT PROOFS of the hard rule: (1) the government's own Ministry of Finance page publishes a stale TT$30,000 cap (a 2009 figure) that CONFLICTS WITH current law — killed 0–3; (2) the repo's contribution tables are stale at 2016 and its benefit rates at 2008, written by an author who KNEW to date them — the architecture was right; the data drifted anyway; (3) NIBTT's OWN SITE IS INTERNALLY INCONSISTENT — its FAQ still states the 2016 rate of 13.2% with no mention of 16.2%, WHILE the TT$13,600 ceiling on that same page is current. One page, one right constant and one wrong one, SILENTLY. THEREFORE: every parameter carries ITS OWN source URL, retrieval date, and review date — provenance is PER-PARAMETER, NOT PER-PAGE. 'Trusting a PAGE is not a strategy.' A staleness check runs in CI, and tests assert every parameter has a date and a source and that no bare numeric constants exist in domain code.

nodes.label: T&T Benchmark Allocation
nodes.rationale: ✅ MARKET-STANDARD, NOT HOUSE STYLE — verified by IDENTICAL match across two independent T&T insurers, PALIG (2012) and Maritime (current): Tax 15% · Loans 25% · Pension/Retirement 10% · Insurance-Life 5% · Insurance-General 5% · Savings+Investment 10% · Living Expense 30%. 'This answers the question I raised about needing a Sagicor fact finder to distinguish convention from house style — IT'S CONVENTION. Encode it as a T&T benchmark with confidence.' Feeds affordability (#5).

nodes.label: PALIG's Quality Rater
nodes.rationale: PALIG scores each category's variance from benchmark: Excellent (better than −5%) · Good (−15% to −6%) · Fair (−30% to −16%) · Poor (−45% to −31%) · Unacceptable (worse than −46%). Worked example: Loans at 34.2% vs a 25% benchmark → variance −9.2% → 'Poor'; Living Expense at 13.2% vs 30% → 'Excellent'. 'A financial health scorecard… it converts the exhaustive budget from data entry into A DIAGNOSIS THE CLIENT RECEIVES. It gives them something back for the work — which is exactly what makes optional homework get done.' Proposed as a new FinancialHealthScore component. 🔴 REPURPOSED, NOT SHIPPED AS DESIGNED (spec §5.1b): PALIG's Excellent→Unacceptable labels GRADE A CLIENT AGAINST A BENCHMARK THEY NEVER AGREED TO, and 'a gentler word doesn't fix that'. DROP the labels and the scorecard; KEEP the variance; EXPRESS IT IN DOLLARS; SURFACE ONLY THE LARGEST — 'Loans take 34% of what you earn. Typical in T&T is 25%. That gap is $1,100 a month.' A FACT, NOT A VERDICT, and it EXPLAINS THE LEAK rather than existing as a separate report card. 'No judgment to hide, so nothing needs hiding.'

nodes.label: Usable Income / The Leak
nodes.rationale: 'PALIG built the leak mechanic in 2012.' Liability/Gross Income 0.537 · Liability/Take-home 0.591 · Usable Income % 0.409 · Usable Income $ 2,925. 'That is OUR leak, computed THIRTEEN YEARS AGO by a T&T insurer. THE MECHANIC IS VALIDATED, NOT NOVEL — which is reassuring rather than disappointing. Ours improves on it by deriving the number CONVERSATIONALLY instead of demanding a filled form.' One of three rationed revelations, selected by triage ('debt' → the leak).

nodes.label: Per-Debt Years-to-Payoff Schedule
nodes.rationale: PALIG tracks each debt with a balance, an end date, and a COMPUTED YEARS-TO-PAYOFF (e.g. Credit Union 1,500 → 2014-11-04 → 1.47 yrs; Mortgage 350,000 → 2016-01-21 → 2.68; Tertiary Education 50,000 → 2015-04-12 → 1.90). 'THIS IS THE INPUT THE LADDERING ENGINE (#11) NEEDS. Obligation declines on a known schedule as debts retire; the term ladder should step down to match. Our spec ASSERTED laddering against declining obligation WITHOUT SAYING WHERE THE DECLINE SCHEDULE COMES FROM. IT COMES FROM HERE.'

nodes.label: Two Competing Needs Methodologies
nodes.rationale: PALIG computes the insurance gap TOP-DOWN FROM NET WORTH (Current Insurance Coverage 350,000 − Net Worth 543,500 = Over/Shortage −193,500). Tatil computes it BOTTOM-UP FROM NEEDS (funeral + loans + income continuation − assets). 'THESE ARE DIFFERENT METHODS AND THEY WILL DISAGREE. Rather than picking one, the engine should support BOTH and SHOW THEM SIDE BY SIDE — two credible numbers WITH A STATED BASIS is more honest than one number with a HIDDEN METHOD, and it's exactly the kind of transparency that BEATS eMONEY'S SILENT-ASSUMPTION PROBLEM.' CAVEAT: insuring to net worth is closer to ESTATE replacement than INCOME replacement, and is arguably THE WEAKER METHOD — present it as a CROSS-CHECK, NOT A HEADLINE (Tatil bottom-up is the headline).

nodes.label: PALIG / Pan-American Life
nodes.rationale: PALIG Personal Net Worth Calculator (2012, last saved 2013) — 'contributes a scoring model and confirms a market convention'. Also markets UL on flexible premiums in T&T (per the knowledge base) — one of the few CONFIRMED facts about T&T universal life. PALIG's contact sheet tracks THREE appointment dates where Guardian documents two — worth confirming with practising agents which is typical. Net worth quality bands (Excellent 1M / Good 750k / Fair 500k / Poor 250k / Unacceptable 100k) are 2012 FIGURES, NEED INFLATION ADJUSTMENT BEFORE REUSE. Disclaimer language worth adopting: 'The calculated results are intended for illustrative purposes only; accuracy is not guaranteed. Please consult a financial professional for advice.'

EXPENSES: Food/Clothing · Education · Entertainment/Travelling · TSTT/WASA/T&TEC/CCTT · Life Insurance Premiums · General Insurance Premiums · Property Maintenance Fee · Reg. Pension/Annuity · Alimony/Maintenance · NIS. nodes.label: The Founder De-Risks the Spec's #1 Risk
nodes.rationale: The repo's README identifies the author as A LICENSED INSURANCE AGENT WITH 13+ YEARS of retirement planning experience. The spec named rate-catalog data as the single HIGH risk — 'outside our control', to be solved by finding a design partner who is ALSO a data supplier. That partner IS the founder: design partner in-house · first user in-house · RATE BOOK SOURCE (an agent has one) · RECOMMENDER OF RECORD already registered with the CBTT · 13 years T&T domain expertise · distribution via five public SEO'd calculators already live. Consequently the spec DOWNGRADES the rate-data risk HIGH → MEDIUM. Mitigation retained regardless: RateProvider interface, seed with ONE carrier and 2–3 products; adding carriers = DATA ENTRY, NOT ENGINEERING; 'DO NOT ATTEMPT TO LAUNCH WITH THE WHOLE MARKET.' The founder's practitioner knowledge also supersedes two agent inferences (annuities under the life licence; the SCP bands) — 'when verification contradicts a practitioner, go to source before overriding them.'
nodes.norm_label: the founder de-risks the spec's #1 risk

nodes.label: Tatil's Four Basic Needs
nodes.rationale: 'A ready-made information architecture.' Tatil frames the entire conversation around four needs: (1) Retirement income; (2) Financial security in event of death; (3) Money to assist in event of critical illness; (4) Money to assist with major expenses (education etc.). 'DO NOT INVENT A NEW FRAMEWORK.' This is the mental model T&T agents are already trained on and clients have already heard — adopting it as the product's IA makes the tool legible to an agent on day one, which is agent ramp (#10) FOR FREE. The spec adopts it as §5.0 and states v1 scope directly in these terms: needs 1 and 2 IN, needs 3 and 4 NEXT — 'two of four is a defensible v1: they are the two largest needs, both engines substantially exist, and triage routes between them, so the architecture doesn't change when 3 and 4 arrive'.

nodes.label: The T&T Needs Formula
nodes.rationale: 'This IS the NeedsEngine spec, from a real T&T insurer' — the formula is NOT INVENTED, it is the standardized T&T instrument Tatil states explicitly. TOTAL NEEDS = funeral cost + medical cost + outstanding loans + mortgage liquidation + rental income for 120 months + education expense + continuation of income until last child attains age 21. TOTAL ASSETS = savings + life insurance + other investments (stocks, shares). TOTAL INSURANCE NEED = TOTAL NEEDS − TOTAL ASSETS. Two conventions worth encoding as NAMED, DATED PARAMETERS: '120 months' of rental income (T&T convention: 10 years) and 'until last child attains 21'. Both are LOCAL NORMS, NOT UNIVERSAL TRUTHS — they belong in ParameterTables, not in code. Correctly omits the US estate-tax liquidity driver.

nodes.label: Budget as Percentage-of-Income Band
nodes.rationale: ⚠️ 'Our spec was WRONG about Budget.' Guardian elicits budget as a PERCENTAGE-OF-INCOME BAND using SOCIAL-PROOF ANCHORING — never as a dollar figure: 'Most of my clients spend between 10–15% of their income towards solving their needs. There are a fortunate few who can invest 16–25%... And some are on a tight budget and can only afford between 5–9%. Into which category would you fall?' THE ENGINEERED ANCHOR: 10–15% is 'most of my clients' (the norm and the default), 16–25% is 'a fortunate few' (aspirational and FLATTERING), 5–9% is 'a tight budget' (the floor). CORRECTION REQUIRED: capture budget as a % band, normalize to TTD internally. The original spec defined it as agent-supplied TTD, WHICH LOSES THE ANCHORING MECHANIC ENTIRELY. All product rates normalize to monthly before optimization regardless of the carrier's native billing frequency.

nodes.label: Three Options, Not One
nodes.rationale: ⚠️ Spec correction. Guardian's Decision Meeting agenda: '3. Presentation of up to three (3) alternative solutions (15 mins) 4. Selecting the solution that has the best benefits for your needs, wants and preferences (10 mins).' The spec had RecommendationEngine → Package; it should be → [Package], THREE of them, with DIFFERENTIATED rationale. 'THE SALE IS A CHOICE AMONG THREE, NOT AN ACCEPT/REJECT OF ONE.' Options must be meaningfully differentiated (e.g. maximum cover / balanced / lowest premium) with distinct rationale, NOT three cosmetic variants.

nodes.label: Two Meetings, Not One Session
nodes.rationale: ⚠️ 'Our spec models a single session. WRONG SHAPE.' Guardian documents the process precisely — Discovery Meeting (~40 min: intro 1 / client intro 2 / importance of income 5 / fact-finding questionnaire 15 / identify needs, wants & budget 15 / summary 1 / list of what to bring / schedule 2nd meeting 1) and Decision Meeting (changes since last meeting 2 / review concerns 2 / three alternative solutions 15 / select solution 10 / paperwork + first premium 5 / schedule medical exam 1 / next steps 1). TWO CONSEQUENCES: (1) THE CLIENT PORTAL'S JOB IS THE GAP BETWEEN THE MEETINGS — not a nice-to-have, its STRUCTURAL role; (2) 'List of what to bring for our 2nd meeting' is WHERE THE POLICY X-RAY LIVES — the agent ALREADY asks clients to bring their policies, so our wedge slots into an existing ritual rather than creating a new one. REFINED IN SPEC §3.3: 'usually two meetings, often three or more' (practitioner confirmation; Guardian documents two, PALIG tracks three) — DO NOT HARDCODE A STEP COUNT. A wizard that ends at step 2 either blocks the real conversation or forces the agent to lie to it. The plan has a STATE, not a step number; the portal is the continuous line, meetings are punctuation; a six-meeting relationship is a supported path, not an error. UNCONFIRMED: whether the sale is typically two (Guardian) or three (PALIG).

nodes.label: Guardian's Triage Checklist
nodes.rationale: 'Triage first — that's how you get to five questions.' Guardian opens with a 16-item concern checklist, self/spouse columns: 'Please tick which is of utmost concern to you currently TO GUIDE OUR DISCUSSION TODAY.' Items: income protection · family income protection · life insurance · critical illness · funeral expense · mortgage planning (repay at term / on death / on critical illness) · paying off debt · retirement · savings · children's education · health · car · property · contents. 'THIS IS THE MECHANISM THAT MAKES FIVE QUESTIONS, NOT TWELVE HONEST. You don't shorten the fact-find by asking less — you TRIAGE FIRST and ask only what's relevant to what they pointed at.' Reduced to ~8 tiles as Screen 0.

nodes.label: Guardian Life of the Caribbean
nodes.rationale: Incumbent whose fact-find instrument supplies the triage checklist, the budget % band anchor, the two-meeting structure, the three-options Decision Meeting agenda, the field-tested soft questions, the informal-dependent question, and a dependents table WITH A HEALTH COLUMN (feeds underwriting pre-qualification #13). ⚠️ Guardian's motivating statistics are FROM 1986 — explicitly labelled as such in their own document. Forty-year-old data is still being presented to clients: 'current, real T&T data is a cheap and genuine differentiator.'

nodes.label: Field-Tested Soft Questions
nodes.rationale: 'The soft questions are written for us — DON'T INVENT THEM.' Guardian's open questions are warm, specific, and already field-tested — the A-mode (one-question-at-a-time) content: 'What are some of the things that you and your family like to do?' · 'What do you believe life insurance should do for you and your family?' · 'If you suffered a long term disability for say 6 to 12 months, how would your bills be paid?' · 'What are some of the things you plan to do when you retire? Paint a picture for me.' · 'How do you feel about University Education for your children? What profession are they leaning towards?'

nodes.label: The Informal-Dependent Question (canvas validation)
nodes.rationale: 'Guardian already asks the informal-dependent question — THE CANVAS IS VALIDATED.' Verbatim: 'If there was an immediate need to fund a major surgery for YOUR PARENTS OR FAMILY MEMBERS due to an accident or sickness, how would you help fund it?' The household obligation (#14) is ALREADY IN THE INCUMBENT'S SCRIPT. 'We're not inventing a need — we're making an existing, awkwardly-worded question visual and structured. That's a much safer bet than a novel insight.' The permission language that makes it work: 'It doesn't have to be official' — the line that lets someone name an outside child or a supported nephew.

nodes.label: Tatil's Suitability + Affordability Attestation
nodes.rationale: 'The suitability attestation ALREADY EXISTS — model ours on it.' Tatil's client signature block: 'I certify that to the best of my knowledge the information provided above is correct. Based on the above review, I understand why the foregoing product(s) have been suggested as suitable for me AND THAT I CAN AFFORD TO PAY THE ONGOING PREMIUMS.' Both client and agent sign, both dated. KEY CONSEQUENCE: it BUNDLES SUITABILITY + AFFORDABILITY in ONE attestation — which is why affordability (#5) CANNOT BE DEFERRED as far as the spec planned; the signed record already asserts it. v1 must at minimum capture monthly income and expense (fact-find Q2) and assert premium sustainability against them.

nodes.label: Tied-Agent Model (confirmed)
nodes.rationale: CONFIRMED IN WRITING from Tatil's own disclaimer. Confirms all three at once: Central Bank regulation (NOT TTSEC), mandatory agent registration, and single-carrier TIED distribution. 'Our segment decision holds' — tied agents first, brokers later; comparison features stay BEHIND A FLAG so we don't offend the first buyer.

nodes.label: The US Textbook Fact Finder (control group)
nodes.rationale: Foundations of Retirement Planning (US textbook template), included deliberately AS CONTRAST. 'It asks about IRAs, Social Security, revocable living trusts, durable powers of attorney, and taxable-equivalent conversion — NONE OF WHICH EXIST IN T&T. It's a precise inventory of WHAT LOCALIZATION MUST STRIP OUT, and it's what every US tool would drag in.'
nodes.norm_label: the us textbook fact finder (control group)

nodes.label: Maritime Financial Group
nodes.rationale: Incumbent fact-find source. Contributes: the benchmark allocation (Taxes 15 · Loans 25 · Retirement 10 · Life 5 · General 5 · Savings 10 · Living 30); emergency fund = 6× GROSS MONTHLY INCOME (note: gross income, NOT months of expenses as in US convention); tax deduction lines (Education Allowance, Company Pension/NIS, Personal Pension, Personal Allowance) mapping onto the TT$60k envelope; the per-debt shape (balance, installment, years to go); and a competitive displacement question listing the client's existing lawyer/accountant/financial advisor then asking 'Are you satisfied with the service? If you like my service will you hire me for the job?'

nodes.label: The Synthesized Five Questions
nodes.rationale: Screen 0 — TRIAGE ('What's on your mind right now?', Guardian's checklist reduced to ~8 tiles, self/spouse; everything downstream adapts). Then five, one at a time, canvas reflecting: (1) Who depends on you? → household canvas, 'A parent, a nephew, someone overseas. It doesn't have to be official.'; (2) What comes in, what goes out? → monthly income AND monthly expense (Tatil captures both; most US tools only capture income); (3) What do you owe? → mortgage, loans, cards: balance, installment, years to go (Maritime's shape); (4) What do you already have? → life insurance, savings, NIS/pension — THIS IS THE X-RAY, seeded from documents where available; (5) What would you want to happen? → one soft question, CHOSEN BY TRIAGE. Then budget — Guardian's % band anchor, VERBATIM. Then: need → gap → 'here's what to bring next time' → portal → Decision Meeting → three options.

nodes.label: TTSEC (Trinidad and Tobago Securities and Exchange Commission)
nodes.rationale: CONFIRMED 3-0: has no robo-adviser-specific rules; regulates automated advice platforms under existing investment-adviser provisions of the Securities Act 2012. CONFIRMED 2-1: robo-adviser entrants subject to the same registration/renewal procedures as investment advisers.
nodes.norm_label: ttsec (trinidad and tobago securities and exchange commission)

nodes.label: Central Bank of Trinidad and Tobago (CBTT)
nodes.rationale: CONFIRMED 3-0: regulated payment-services perimeter covers money transfer, payment instruments, clearance/settlement, e-money, wallets, remittances; PSPs register under s.36(cc) Central Bank Act Chap. 79:02. CONFIRMED 3-0: the list does NOT enumerate read-only account aggregation — an argument from omission on the regulator's own page. One claim REFUTED 1-2 (that the perimeter is exactly two categories via GoAnywhere Portal).
nodes.norm_label: central bank of trinidad and tobago (cbtt)

nodes.label: Securities Act 2012 (Chap. 83:02)
nodes.rationale: CONFIRMED 3-0 as the basis on which TTSEC regulates automated advice: 'No specific guidelines for robo-advisers exist locally, however the provisions for investment advisers within the Securities Act (as amended) 2012, provide the basis for regulating potential market entrants.' The key design line: 'investment advice' covers SECURITIES ONLY — budgeting, cash-flow projection, NIS/pension modeling, insurance needs analysis, and goal tracking sit outside s.51. Registration as an investment adviser requires TT$50,000 minimum capital and By-law 19 prerequisites.

nodes.label: Data Protection Act 2011 (Chap. 22:04)
nodes.rationale: CONFIRMED 3-0: only Part I (ss.1-6, General Privacy Principles) plus administrative ss.7-18, 22, 23, 25(1), 26, 28 came into force 6 January 2012. The rest — including Part IV (private-sector obligations, ss.69-83) — is NOT proclaimed. LIVE RULE: s.6 binds all persons handling personal information, and s.6(l) requires that information disclosed outside T&T go only to jurisdictions with comparable safeguards — this is the cloud-hosting constraint, in force today. EU/UK (GDPR) reads as comparable; US-only hosting is a harder argument. FUTURE: s.69 would capture the app even if hosted abroad — build to Part IV now, proclamation is a switch someone can flip. One claim REFUTED 0-3: that s.72 makes cross-border transfer consent-based rather than adequacy-based.

nodes.label: Caribbean Bank Aggregation Coverage Gap
nodes.rationale: RESOLVED — there is none, unambiguously. Salt Edge: zero Caribbean coverage (Americas = Argentina, Brazil, Canada, Mexico only, 10 connections). Plaid: zero (~20 countries, North America/UK/Europe). CONFIRMED 3-0 that Republic Bank, First Citizens, Scotiabank Trinidad, RBC Caribbean and ANSA Bank cannot be connected through either. No developer portals confirmed at any of 43 T&T institutions. Strategic read: the constraint IS the positioning — don't sell 'we aggregate your accounts', sell 'planning that works without aggregation'. eMoney's own users complain aggregation is broken anyway. Open: Yodlee/Envestnet, MX, Flinks not individually verified.

nodes.label: Finerio Connect / Ozone API / Visa Open-Banking Toolkit
nodes.rationale: CONFIRMED 3-0: June 2022, Finerio Connect + Ozone API + Visa announced an end-to-end open-banking toolkit explicitly targeting financial institutions across Latin America and the Caribbean — a white-label modular stack via the Finerio API Hub. CONFIRMED 2-1: includes account aggregation supplied by Finerio Connect, plus data handling and a PFM app. CAVEAT: sold TO BANKS so they can offer open banking — not a ready-made consumer-side aggregator with live T&T bank connections. Whether any T&T bank has adopted it is UNVERIFIED and determines whether this path is real.
nodes.norm_label: finerio connect / ozone api / visa open-banking toolkit

nodes.label: Software-as-Advice Perimeter
nodes.rationale: RESOLVED, and the most consequential finding of Round 2 — Round 1's hedge ('automated recommendations COULD fall within scope') is gone. Automated advice does not escape the perimeter by being software: a robo-adviser entrant must itself register as an investment adviser. The line is at SECURITIES-SPECIFIC recommendations — asset allocation, fund selection, buy/sell/hold. Two postures: (a) stay outside, ship planning/projection/education and let the registered advisor supply the securities recommendation — fastest, no vendor registration; (b) cross deliberately and register (TT$50,000 minimum capital, By-law 19). RECOMMENDATION: (a) first, architected so (b) is a later switch — keep the recommendation layer separable from the planning engine.

nodes.label: TTSEC Review of Algorithms and Methodologies
nodes.rationale: CONFIRMED 3-0 via real TTSEC precedent: a 2018 research paper, 'Automated Advice Tools in the Securities Industry of Trinidad and Tobago: The Regulatory Challenges', identifying six focus areas — fiduciary standard of care, client profiling/on-boarding, REVIEW OF ALGORITHMS AND METHODOLOGIES, suitability of recommendations, conflicts of interest, effective compliance programmes. Point 3 is the one to internalize: TTSEC expects to review your algorithms. Build the engine explainable and auditable from day one — assumption provenance, versioned calculation logic, reproducible outputs. A design constraint, not a compliance afterthought.
nodes.norm_label: ttsec review of algorithms and methodologies

nodes.label: TTSEC 2024 Fintech-Policy Paper (unverified leads)
nodes.rationale: UNVERIFIED — 3 claims died on a session limit, NOT on merit. Treat as leads, not findings: (1) fintech providers doing a regulated activity must register under an existing category (investment adviser, broker-dealer, underwriter, SRO, issuer); (2) the paper explicitly names 'Automated Advice Tools' — INCLUDING financial aggregator platforms that link accounts across institutions and mine the data to provide investment advice — as within TTSEC's regulatory scoping; if confirmed, this describes the exact product architecture; (3) TTSEC concluded it can regulate fintech under existing law without amendment, and offers a combined Innovation Hub + Regulatory Sandbox as a pre-registration engagement path. The sandbox lead is worth chasing independently — a defined path to talk to the regulator before committing to an architecture is worth a lot.

nodes.label: eMoney 'Confidence Age' Metric
nodes.rationale: CONFIRMED 3-0: a proprietary metric — the age at which a client's Monte Carlo probability-of-success score dips below the advisor's chosen threshold for a strong plan. Reveals the engine shape: a WHOLE-PLAN Monte Carlo score projected across the client's lifetime, not a point-in-time estimate, surfaced as an AGE — far more legible than '83% success'. Worth copying the pattern, not the metric name. Unresolved: trial count, return-assumption methodology (historical bootstrap vs parametric), per-goal probabilities. You don't need them: pick a defensible methodology (1,000+ trials, regime-aware or historical-bootstrap returns) and document it. Being MORE transparent than eMoney is a differentiator.

nodes.label: NIBTT (National Insurance Board of Trinidad and Tobago)
nodes.rationale: Issuing agency for NIS contribution and benefit rates. Site hygiene is demonstrably poor: publishes retirement/invalidity benefit rates in two unreconciled locations with different values; the FAQ page (cont_FAQs-rev.html) still states the 2016 13.2% rate while the TT$13,600 ceiling on the same page is current. Verified by direct scrape 2026-07-16.
nodes.norm_label: nibtt (national insurance board of trinidad and tobago)

nodes.label: Increment Mechanic (1 increment per 25 contributions above 750)
nodes.rationale: CONFIRMED 3-0 from NIBTT verbatim: 'For every block of 25 contributions paid in excess of 750 one increment is added to the basic pension rate.' Formula structure confirmed as basic + floor(excess/25) x increment. Corroborated independently by the June 2022 NIS training transcript. Untouched by the 2026 reform.
nodes.norm_label: increment mechanic (1 increment per 25 contributions above 750)

nodes.label: TT$3,000 Minimum Retirement Pension
nodes.rationale: CONFIRMED 3-0, effective 1 February 2012, verbatim: 'the board shall pay with effect from February 1, 2012 the sum of $3,000.00 monthly'. A challenge claiming the minimum attaches to the grant rather than the pension was REFUTED 0-3. Unindexed for 14 years; the 9th Actuarial Review explicitly recommended holding it there. SIGNIFICANCE REDUCED BY THE 2016 TABLE: under 2008 basics every class was below it (hence the now-STRUCK '20 years to beat the floor' claim); under 2016 basics classes XIII-XVI exceed it without increments (3,256.50 / 3,607.50 / 3,938.00 / 4,079.40). Still binds for classes I-XII, which is most contributors.

nodes.label: Age 60-64 Cessation Rule
nodes.rationale: Confirmed from source: age 60-64 requires ceasing insurable employment to claim; age 65 is paid whether you retire or not. Once claimed at 60-64, the pension continues even if the person returns to insurable employment before 65. Payment starts from the Monday of the week retirement age was reached and continues monthly for life.

nodes.label: Era-Selected Contribution Rates
nodes.rationale: CONFIRMED and SURVIVES the discrediting of nibtt-authoritative-rates.md. Contribution rates are published as dated historical sets (1972-2006, 2008-2012, 2013-2014, 2016 at 13.2%, 2026 at 16.2%), each applying to contributions PAID during its era. The 2016 page remains live because contributions paid Sept 2016 -> Jan 2026 were made at 13.2% — current for its period, not stale. The repo's HISTORICAL_EARNINGS_TABLES + getTableForDate() implements this correctly.

nodes.label: Claim-Date-Keyed Benefit Rates
nodes.rationale: CONFIRMED and SURVIVES the discrediting of nibtt-authoritative-rates.md. Decisive sitemap wording: 'Rates of constant Care and Attendance Allowance for persons QUALIFYING ON OR AFTER 7th January 2008.' Benefit rates key to the date you QUALIFY, not the dates you contributed — one table applied at claim time. So the repo's single-table PENSION_RATES is the architecturally correct SHAPE; only the VALUES are stale. Note this cuts both ways: a history of benefit tables does exist, confirming a claimant gets the schedule in force at qualification (2016).

nodes.label: Practitioner Knowledge as Evidence
nodes.rationale: Principle: when verification contradicts a domain practitioner, the practitioner is EVIDENCE — go to source before overriding them. Repeatedly borne out: the founder was right about Class Z's meaning, right about SCP bands, right about NIS counting as assessed income, right that era-selection was deliberate, and right to point at the rates section where the current 2016 benefit table actually lives. Also the sole evidence on the annuity-scope question — reasonable grounds to proceed, not grounds to stop asking. Companion principle: a code smell is a hypothesis, not a finding.

nodes.label: NIS Retirement/Invalidity Benefit Table (eff. 2008-01-07)
nodes.rationale: STALE. Class I basic 335.83/mo incr 4.90; Class XVI basic 2,475.70/mo incr 46.76. Effective 2008-01-07. This is the table the repo's PENSION_RATES encodes and the one NIBTT's own Benefits section still serves — the trap. Confirmed to have run through 2013 by the 2014 PDF printing 2013 and 2014 side by side with the 2013 column equal to the 2008 table. Publishes both basics AND increments.

nodes.label: NIS Basic Retirement and Invalidity Pension Rates 2016 (eff. 2016-09-05)
nodes.rationale: CURRENT and CONFIRMED. Class I basic 566.72/mo; Class XVI basic 4,079.40/mo — roughly 69% above the 2008 basics. Effective 2016-09-05. Publishes basics ONLY ('New Basic Pension'). Lives under /Contribution_Rates/ rather than the Benefits section, which is why a single-page scrape missed it. Blocking action: update PENSION_RATES to these values before any retirement figure ships.
nodes.norm_label: nis basic retirement and invalidity pension rates 2016 (eff. 2016-09-05)

nodes.label: NIBTT Benefit-Rate Revision History (2012 / 2013 / 2014 / 2016)
nodes.rationale: NIBTT publishes each revision showing ONLY WHAT CHANGED on a separate dated page. Basics: 335.83 (2008-13) -> 419.79 (2014) -> 566.72 (2016) for Class I; 2,475.70 -> 2,983.76 -> 4,079.40 for Class XVI. Increments: 4.90 (2008) -> 6.11 (2013) -> unpublished. This history is visible from the rates index but NOT from the Benefits index — one missing link produced total confidence in a wrong answer.

nodes.label: Unresolved 2016 Increment Values
nodes.rationale: UNVERIFIED — deliberately not resolved by inference. No 2016 increment table is published. Reading (a): 2013 increments still stand (Class I 6.11, Class XVI 56.33), fitting the 'publish only what changed' pattern. Reading (b): increments were revised in 2016 but not published. Reading (a) is the more natural fit, but the project has twice been burned by a plausible inference, so this must be confirmed with NIBTT directly or from Legal Notices 25-30 under Amendments/NIBTTAct_amend.html before the pension formula ships. BLOCKING.

nodes.label: 'Top Earner Needs 20 Years to Beat the Floor' Claim
nodes.rationale: STRUCK / FALSE under current rates. Derived from the stale 2008 table: (3,000 - 2,475.70) / 46.76 = 11.2 -> 12 increments -> 300 contributions beyond 750 = 1,050 total, ~20 years. Was billed as 'the strongest client-facing insight in the project so far'. Under the 2016 basics Class XVI is 4,079.40, already above the minimum, so the claim collapses. The dramatic framing was an artifact of the stale table — a caution against building client-facing narrative on an undated constant.
nodes.norm_label: 'top earner needs 20 years to beat the floor' claim

nodes.label: Class Z (Employment-Injury-Only Contribution)
nodes.rationale: CONFIRMED from source (Rate Amendments, verbatim): employer-paid contributions for employment injury coverage for an employed person under 16, or in receipt of retirement pension, or aged 65+; unpaid apprentice $1.00/week. Buys employment-injury cover only — which is why it is ~5% of a full contribution: no further retirement benefit accrues. Exactly as the founder described. Initially flagged 'do not encode until confirmed' when no definition could be found.

nodes.label: Class Z Class XVI Site Typo (220.72 vs 20.72)
nodes.rationale: RESOLVED as an error on NIBTT's own page. Class Z is exactly 5.00% of the total weekly contribution for classes I-XV (e.g. XV: 20.00 / 399.90). Class XVI should be 414.30 x 0.05 = 20.72; the page prints 220.72 — a stray leading '2'. Encode 20.72, flag the discrepancy, do not propagate NIBTT's typo. Initially flagged as 'wildly out of pattern (~53%)' with the meaning unknown.
nodes.norm_label: class z class xvi site typo (220.72 vs 20.72)

nodes.label: Pre-1999 Earnings-Class Restructuring
nodes.rationale: From rates.html Rate Amendments. Benefit periods 1980-08-11 -> 1999-05-02: old classes 1-4 map to new Class 1; 5->2; 6->3; 7->4; 8->5; classes 6-16 are new. Benefit periods before 1980-08-11 (from 1999-05-03): old classes 1-6 -> new Class 1; 7->2; 8->3. Relevant to any client with contributions before 1999 — i.e. anyone retiring now with a long career.

nodes.label: Mis-Selling Exposure from Understated NIS
nodes.rationale: The causal chain, and it runs in the SELF-SERVING direction: understated NIS pension -> client looks poorer in retirement -> retirement gap overstated -> engine recommends more product. On a suitability record the client signs, this is a real mis-selling exposure. BLOCKING: must be fixed before any retirement figure ships. The sharpest irony of the episode: the scrape-based 'correction' would have preserved the mis-selling bug in the name of correctness, having reasoned that the invented defect was suspiciously self-serving.

nodes.label: Scrape-the-Issuer Rule
nodes.rationale: The rule as first stated: search-and-verify is for questions with no authoritative publisher; when an agency publishes the number, scrape the agency; do not verify a number against search results when the issuer publishes it. THEN CORRECTED BY EXPERIENCE: scraping is not verification either. A single page is a SAMPLE, not the issuer's position. When a number is disputed, find EVERY page the issuer publishes it on and reconcile them — because agencies contradict themselves, and NIBTT demonstrably does. Three compounding errors produced the false 'fabrication' verdict: searched one branch of the site and concluded the whole site; mistook 'I could not find it' for 'it does not exist'; accused a correct source of fabricating. The lecture was right; the lecturer failed it.

nodes.label: Tenth Actuarial Valuation of the National Insurance System (as of 30 June 2016)
nodes.author: ILO
nodes.rationale: The most recent published actuarial review — an ILO report to the National Insurance Board, valuation date 30 June 2016, published ~2019. Scraped from nibtt.net 2026-07-16. CRITICAL CAVEAT: its projections are conditional and dated; the 2026 reforms (16.2% rate, retirement age 60->65) came AFTER it and change the projections. Quoting 'NIS runs out in 2035' as current fact misuses the source. The only fair framing is 'the most recent published actuarial review projects X under stated assumptions, and the reforms since respond to it.'
nodes.norm_label: tenth actuarial valuation of the national insurance system (as of 30 june 2016)

nodes.label: NIS Asset Exhaustion Projection (2035-36)
nodes.rationale: 10th review base scenario: expenditure exceeds contributions 2016-17; exceeds contributions plus investment income (assets start to fall) 2023-24; assets exhausted 2035-36. With the recommended 16.2% alone, exhaustion moves to 2042-43. With the full three-part package, assets start to decrease 2043-44 and are exhausted 2053-54. DECAYING FACT — never present the exhaustion date without noting the reforms since; never say 'NIS will run out in 2035'.

nodes.label: General Average Premium (GAP) 25.5%
nodes.rationale: The contribution rate needed to fund all benefits over the projection period, per the 10th review. The legal rate at valuation was 13.2%. Actuary verbatim: 'This contribution rate is considerably higher than the current legal contribution rate of 13.2 per cent. This conclusion is not new, it is the same as in previous actuarial valuations. However, the magnitude and the time passed make this recommendation more urgent today.' The 2027 step to 19.2% still sits well below it. Migration sensitivity moves GAP only 25.5 -> 24.8.

nodes.label: The Actuary's Three-Part Reform Package
nodes.rationale: The 16.2% rate was ONE LEG of a three-part package; the others were early-retirement factors and freezing pensions in payment for five years. Only with all three does exhaustion move to 2053-54. Pensions in payment were NOT frozen, so the enacted reform is a partial implementation of a package the actuary presented as a whole. A materially important nuance that cuts AGAINST over-claiming: the rate rise did happen and it does push the date out. Actuary verbatim: 'This recommendation is however not enough to restore financial sustainability over the long term. Further contribution increases will be necessary.'

nodes.label: Structural Facts vs Projections (Durability Rule)
nodes.rationale: Design principle for client-facing output: prefer STRUCTURAL facts (ceiling, minimum, whole-life averaging, demographics) over PROJECTIONS — structural facts don't decay. Durable evidence: minimum annual asset return avoiding a negative reserve within 50 years is 12.9%, 'considerably higher than the best-estimate assumption'; return sensitivity moves exhaustion by only +/-1 year (2035 at 5.25% yield -> 2037 at 6.25%); migration leaves the exhaustion year unaffected; contributor-to-pensioner ratio falls 3.7:1 -> 1.1:1 over 50 years with pensioners rising 135,049 -> 353,255 (demographic, not political). The point: NIS's funding problem cannot be invested out of, migrated out of, or grown out of. Honest framing: 'NIS is a floor, not a plan.'

nodes.label: Ninth Actuarial Review (AR2013, published June 2015)
nodes.rationale: A useful control: its recommendations were largely implemented, evidence the actuary's advice does eventually land. Raise MIE $12,000 -> $13,600 (implemented); rate -> 13.2% in 2016 (implemented); maintain minimum pension at $3,000 (still $3,000, 14 years unindexed); retirement age 60 -> 65 over 2025-2060 (implemented FASTER, 2028-2036); auto-adjust MIE/minimum pension/rate (NOT implemented).

nodes.label: Missing 11th Actuarial Review
nodes.rationale: OPEN. The site lists 7th-10th only. The 10th uses 2016 data published ~2019 — meaning the most recent public valuation is a decade old and predates the reforms it prompted. The 2026 reform's rate rise and age change must rest on a newer, possibly unpublished valuation; finding it would supersede the sustainability analysis entirely. If no 11th exists, that is itself notable.

nodes.label: National Insurance Act (and Amendments)
nodes.rationale: NOT YET READ. Legal Notices 25-30 under Amendments/NIBTTAct_amend.html are the identified route to resolving the 2016 increment values — the blocking unknown for the pension formula. Confirmed NOT amended by Finance Bill 2026, so 2026 NIS changes came via regulations or Orders.

nodes.label: TT$13,600/month Insurable Earnings Ceiling
nodes.rationale: CONFIRMED 3-0 and current. Class XVI floor. Earnings above it still contribute at Class XVI but do NOT increase the pension — a hard benefit ceiling for high earners. Raised from $12,000 on the 9th Actuarial Review's recommendation. Notable provenance case: the ceiling is CURRENT on the same NIBTT FAQ page that carries the STALE 13.2% rate. Untouched by the 2026 reform. A structural (non-decaying) fact, safe for client-facing use.

nodes.label: Whole-Life Earnings Averaging
nodes.rationale: RESOLVED from the June 2022 NIBTT training transcript, officer verbatim: 'it's not based on your last value of contributions, but your average value throughout your lifetime'. Independently corroborated by NIS Pension Calculation Research.md. The repo's averageLifetimeMonthlyEarnings = totalLifetimeIncomeSum / totalContribMonths is CORRECT. The flagged concern that it understates a rising earner was unfounded as a bug — it understates relative to final salary, but that IS the rule. Sets the AMOUNT; the 5-of-7-years rule gates ELIGIBILITY. A structural fact, safe for client-facing use.

nodes.label: NIS Qualifying Conditions (150/50 or 5-of-7 years)
nodes.rationale: From the training transcript: (1) 150 total contributions with 50 in the last 3 years, OR (2) employed 5 of the last 7 years; and (3) 750 contributions minimum for a pension. Resolves where the project's '7 years' memory came from — it is a QUALIFYING window, not an averaging window. Two different rules, easily conflated; the engine must implement both separately.

nodes.label: Parameter Drift
nodes.rationale: The project's recurring failure mode, demonstrated inside its own working notes: five sources, five different Class XVI monthly pensions spanning ~5x. NIS Pension Calculation Research.md $6,799 (50%-of-earnings method — its own text says 'appears to be approximately 50%', an inference not a rule); NIS Pension Amounts - Corrected.md $5,500 (no methodology, no source, titled 'Corrected' which implies authority it doesn't document); NIS_Research_Findings.md $10,000-12,000 (self-labelled 'estimated', implausible); repo PENSION_RATES $2,475.70 (2008); NIBTT current $4,079.40 (2016). None should be encoded. The authoritative chain is: NIBTT published benefit schedule (dated) -> basic + increments per class -> lifetime-average class lookup.

nodes.label: PENSION_RATES / Earnings-Table Internal Inconsistency
nodes.rationale: Precisely diagnosed: not merely 'obsolete' but MISMATCHED. HISTORICAL_EARNINGS_TABLES holds 12 dated snapshots (1972->2016), era-selected via getTableForDate() — correct by design. PENSION_RATES is one table with no date and no comment holding 2008-schedule values, while classification uses the 2016 earnings table. So the code CLASSIFIES against 2016 bands and PAYS at 2008 rates — a genuine internal inconsistency regardless of which schedule is right. PENSION_RATES lacks the date and source its twelve neighbours carry.

nodes.label: 750-Contribution Threshold
nodes.rationale: CONFIRMED 3-0: 750+ contributions -> lifetime pension; below -> Retirement Grant. May include paid, Voluntary, Age Credits and/or Benefit Credits — the credit types are new to the project and mean the engine's contribution count is not just paid weeks. Training transcript: 'it doesn't matter when, throughout your lifetime, you would have accumulated this.' The 8th Actuarial Review recommended cutting it to 260 weeks; not implemented. Untouched by the 2026 reform.

nodes.label: NIS Retirement Grant
nodes.rationale: CONFIRMED 3-0: one-time lump sum for fewer than 750 contributions, equal to 3x the monetary value of total contributions, minimum TT$3,000, for those reaching retirement age on/after 2008-01-07. Excluded from SCP assessed income by inference (not monthly income) — the SCP Act would confirm by law. Untouched by the 2026 reform.

nodes.label: NIS Contribution Rate 16.2% (eff. 2026-01-05)
nodes.rationale: CONFIRMED 3-0: effective 5 January 2026, up from 13.2%, split one-third employee / two-thirds employer. The 10th Actuarial Valuation recommended exactly this rate starting July 2019 — it arrived six and a half years late, and the actuary said plainly it would not be enough on its own.

nodes.label: 19.2% January 2027 Rate (PROVISIONAL)
nodes.rationale: PROVISIONAL, vote 2-1. Rests on a Ministry of Finance budget announcement plus arithmetic inference (16.2 + 3), NOT on any NIBTT-published or gazetted earnings-class schedule. The 2027 class tables do not yet exist in published form, so any 2027 table is necessarily derived. Flag as PROVISIONAL in code; do not present 2027 figures to clients as settled. Still well below the 25.5% GAP.

nodes.label: NIS 16 Earnings Classes (I-XVI)
nodes.rationale: CONFIRMED 3-0: 16 classes. Class I $867-1,472.99/mo, assumed AWE $270, $43.80/wk total at 16.2%; Class XVI $13,600+/mo, assumed AWE $3,138, $508.50/wk ($169.50 ee / $339.00 er) at 16.2%. The 2016 columns show 13.2% figures (Class I $35.70, Class XVI $414.30) — superseded, though the bands and assumed AWE stand. The 16-class structure survives the 2026 changes intact.

nodes.label: Eighth Actuarial Review (published Sept 2012, valuation 30 June 2010)
nodes.rationale: Recommended converting the earnings-class system to career-average revalued earnings (CARE) and — conditional on that — cutting the pension threshold from 750 to 260 weeks. NEITHER was implemented. Useful twice over: it confirms the current architecture is stable, and it names the reform that would invalidate large parts of the engine if it ever lands.
nodes.norm_label: eighth actuarial review (published sept 2012, valuation 30 june 2010)

nodes.label: 2026 NIS Reform Scope (rate + retirement age only)
nodes.rationale: CONFIRMED 3-0: the reform changed EXACTLY TWO things — the contribution rate (13.2 -> 16.2 -> 19.2) and the retirement age (60 -> 65, +1yr every 2yrs from Jan 2028, reaching 65 in 2036). It did NOT touch the 750 threshold, increments, minimum pension, grant formula, or ceiling. Valuable negative evidence: it bounds the blast radius of the reform on the engine.
nodes.norm_label: 2026 nis reform scope (rate + retirement age only)

nodes.label: Health Surcharge
nodes.rationale: CONFIRMED 3-0: TT$8.25/wk above TT$469.99/mo, TT$4.80/wk otherwise. Exemptions CONFIRMED 3-0: under 16, 60 and over, or only income is pension. The age-60 exemption is material — a retirement-planning app that charges Health Surcharge to a 62-year-old is simply wrong, and the repo's constants alone don't capture it (the exemptions are a separate rule). Boundary note: IRD says 'sixty (60) years and over'; one secondary source renders it 'over 60' — IRD's wording governs, confirm against Health Surcharge Act Chap. 75:05. Do NOT cross-wire with the NIS 'under 16 / 65 and over' Class Z rule — different levy. Not amended by Finance Bill 2026.

nodes.label: TT$60,000 Combined Deduction Cap
nodes.rationale: CONFIRMED 3-0. The Ministry of Finance page's TT$30,000 is a stale 2009 figure that CONFLICTS WITH current law — one of the three government stale-document instances underpinning the per-parameter provenance rule. Confirmed NOT touched by Finance Bill 2026.

nodes.label: TT$90,000 Personal Allowance
nodes.rationale: UNVERIFIED — negative evidence only. Finance Bill 2026 doesn't change it, which does NOT establish that it is right. Must be verified affirmatively, not by absence of change. Same status as the 25%/30% PAYE bands and TT$1M threshold.

nodes.label: 70% NIS Deductibility
nodes.rationale: ENTIRELY UNVERIFIED. Confirmed only that Finance Bill 2026 does not touch it. Flagged for affirmative verification.

nodes.label: Income Tax Act Chap. 75:01
nodes.rationale: The statute Finance Bill 2026 amends — only via s.8, new s.18D, s.28(9), and new s.48O. Negative evidence: the Bill does not touch the personal allowance, PAYE rates/threshold, 70% NIS deductibility, the TT$60k cap, or s.134(6).

nodes.label: Finance Bill 2026 (House Bill 12 of 2026)
nodes.rationale: IT IS ONLY A BILL. Laid 5 June 2026, passed the House 28-0 (13 abstentions). Senate passage and Presidential assent COULD NOT BE VERIFIED as of July 2026. Code as conditional on assent, with the retroactive 1 Jan 2026 effective date. Valuable negative evidence: it does not amend the National Insurance Act, the Senior Citizens' Pension Act, or the Health Surcharge Act — so any 2026 change to NIS/SCP/surcharge came from regulations or Orders, not this Bill. Also contains cll. 4-5 (Prison Service Act 5th Sch.; Police Service Regs reg. 183A — protective-services superannuation on acting-office salary), a lead on the unverified public servants' pension formula.

nodes.label: Income Tax Act s.8(1)(ta) — Approved Deferred Annuity Exemption
nodes.rationale: NEW via Finance Bill 2026, conditional on assent. Exempts income from an approved deferred annuity plan (s.28) from income tax, effective 1 Jan 2026 — CONDITIONAL ON the annuity being purchased by a T&T resident and maturing between ages 50 and 70. Refines an earlier Round 1 finding that stated the exemption more loosely.
nodes.norm_label: income tax act s.8(1)(ta) — approved deferred annuity exemption

nodes.label: Income Tax Act s.8(1)(tb) — Approved Pension Fund Plan Exemption
nodes.rationale: NEW via Finance Bill 2026, conditional on assent. Parallel exemption to s.8(1)(ta), for approved pension fund plan income.
