nodes.rationale: US precedent cited as the outcome of optimistic-illustration framing: ~251,000 policyholders, US$55M settlement. Invoked to establish that the Cashbuilder III 10.5%-vs-4% marketing language is a recognised litigation-grade pattern, not a hypothetical.

nodes.label: Cashbuilder I (CBI)
nodes.rationale: UNVERIFIED — referenced only as 'CBI', a further legacy Cashbuilder generation. No specification obtained. Listed among the open items on Cashbuilder.

nodes.label: Tax Envelope Optimizer
nodes.rationale: The engine feature that allocates contributions across tax-advantaged envelopes. Would be materially wrong to ignore s.134(6A) if the one-third-of-income rule is still current, since that is a far larger allowance for high earners than the TT$60,000 cap.

nodes.label: Tatil Life
nodes.rationale: The seed carrier. Source of the Commission Schedule V5 (provided by founder), the Four Basic Needs framework, the standardized needs formula, and the suitability attestation. CBTT-regulated; agents registered with CBTT and only authorised to sell Tatil Life products — a TIED-AGENT model, confirmed in writing. First milestone is one household, ONE CARRIER, three products.

nodes.label: The Commission Firewall
nodes.source_location: THE DESIGN DECISION THIS FILE FORCES
nodes.rationale: 🔴 'The single most important integrity rule in the system' / 'may be the most important trust feature in the product.' THE RULE (non-negotiable): the recommendation engine MUST NOT SEE COMMISSION. Commission is NOT an input to RecommendationEngine. It is computed AFTER the recommendation is fixed, for the agent's own economics only, and NEVER influences ranking, selection, or the three options presented. WHY: 1st-year commission for products solving the SAME need ranges Whole Life 60% · 20-Yr Convertible Term 35% · LifeSpan Lite 30% · Platinum Edge 0.5% — a whole life pays the agent 120× a Platinum Edge. An engine that optimizes for commission even slightly or implicitly steers every client to whole life: textbook mis-selling, violates the Market Conduct Guideline, and is the exact 'silent modeling error' failure mode positioned against eMoney. ARCHITECTURE: RecommendationEngine optimizes coverage-adequacy-per-premium-dollar FOR THE CLIENT; a separate downstream CommissionCalculator tells the agent what they'll earn on a recommendation ALREADY MADE. The two never touch — the deterministic-core / separable-layer discipline applied to its highest-stakes case. AND IT BECOMES A FEATURE: the SuitabilityRecord can affirmatively state the recommendation was made without reference to commission (a Market Conduct gold standard, a defensible answer to 'why this product?'); an optional agent-initiated commission-transparency mode (radical transparency as a post-CLICO differentiator); and the engine can FLAG ITS OWN TEMPTATION — 'a whole life here pays you 60% vs 35% on term — but term is the better fit' — turning the tool into the agent's integrity backstop. OPEN: whether to surface commission to the CLIENT by default; leaning agent-initiated only.

nodes.label: Commission Heaping
nodes.source_location: What the commission structure itself teaches
nodes.rationale: Nearly everything front-loads year 1 (Whole Life 60% → 15% → 10% → 5% → 5% → 2.5%). This is WHY persistency/lapse prevention (#4) matters so much: an early lapse means the agent keeps a large advance the insurer clawed back, and the client loses everything. 'The commission shape IS the lapse-prevention argument.' Used as DOMAIN UNDERSTANDING, never as a ranking input. Related teachings: annuities/investment products pay little DELIBERATELY (Destiny Option 1 5%, Platinum Edge 0.5%, Publicsaver savings 5% level) — low commission SIGNALS a savings vehicle, not a protection product, and is exactly why an honest engine must recommend them freely despite the low payout; age-banding on Cashbuilder/Riders (35% at 0–50 down to 20% at 61+) reflects real underwriting economics; single-premium rows (1.5–2.5%, no renewal) distinguish lump-sum from regular-premium business in the data model.

nodes.label: LifeSpan Lite
nodes.rationale: Term to 60/70. Simplified issue (no bonus, lower commission — 30% yr 1) — 'the easy-issue protection play'.

nodes.label: Publicsaver (Life / DA)
nodes.rationale: Publicsaver Life is a HYBRID split into a savings portion + an insurance portion, the two commissioned SEPARATELY (savings 5%/yr, insurance 35% yr1). Publicsaver DA is a savings-oriented deferred annuity. ⚠️ UNVERIFIED: mechanics need confirmation from a product brochure — 'we have economics, not features'. Listed under Open confirmations in both the catalog and the knowledge base.

nodes.label: Platinum Edge
nodes.rationale: Age 0–75. Flat 0.5%/yr commission — 120× LESS first-year commission than whole life for a product that can solve the same need, which is the arithmetic that forces the commission firewall. LIKELY single-premium / investment-oriented permanent — ⚠️ INFERRED, not confirmed: mechanics need a product brochure; the commission schedule shows economics, not features.

nodes.label: Tatil Product Specifications (research doc)
nodes.rationale: Highest-quality product source in the project: derived from Tatil Life's own internal 'Product Training and Specifications' folder plus tatil.co.tt. Authoritative — supersedes the US/generic material in product-knowledge-base.md for anything Tatil-specific. Verification status is mixed: Destiny, Platinum Edge, SPIA, Whole Life 2023, Rest Assured 2024 and Endowment 2024 are read from actual spec docs (verified); Cashbuilder II/III and GoldSpoon are scanned image PDFs NOT YET READ (unverified, need OCR/vision).

nodes.label: Destiny — Individual Retirement Solution
nodes.rationale: Verbatim spec: 'a Universal Life product, with a fund portion only, and no insurance component' — a pure accumulation vehicle with NO premium loadings, so every dollar paid enters the fund (an improvement on the predecessor which took front-end loadings). CORRECTION to earlier work: the product knowledge base filed Destiny under 'deferred annuity with fund options' — right in effect but it understates that the chassis is UL. Variants: Individual/Corporate x Registered(BIR)/Unregistered; Corporate is Registered-only. Issue ages Registered 18-60, Unregistered 1-65. Min monthly premium $200; min lump sum $500 individual / $1,000 corporate. Death benefit = the Accumulation. Partial withdrawals NOT allowed on BIR-approved policies; Unregistered up to 90% of cash value. Rider: Total Disability Waiver of Premium (ATDWP 6); term coverage on Unregistered only. Source: Tatil spec 'TL Individual Retirement Solution — 2023' (verified/authoritative).

nodes.label: Destiny Investment Option 1 (2% guarantee / 5% commission)
nodes.rationale: Moderately Low risk. Guaranteed minimum interest 2% pa — the strongest guarantee of the three. Equities <=20%, Government bonds <=55%. Commission: year 1 = 5%, year 2 = 3%, year 3+ = 1%. The best guarantee for the client pays the agent the least.

nodes.label: Destiny Investment Option 2 (1% guarantee / 12% commission)
nodes.rationale: Moderate risk. Guaranteed minimum interest 1% pa. Equities <=30%, Government bonds <=45%. Commission: year 1 = 12%, year 2 = 5%, year 3+ = 0.25% of fund.

nodes.label: Destiny Investment Option 3 (0% guarantee / 12% commission)
nodes.rationale: Moderately High risk. Guaranteed minimum interest 0% pa — guarantees nothing. Equities <=40%, Government bonds <=25%. Commission: year 1 = 12%, year 2 = 5%, year 3+ = 0.25% of fund. Interacts with the 200bp investment margin spread: a year returning under 2% gross credits ZERO. Any engine that can see commission will drift toward this option.

nodes.label: Destiny Commission Conflict of Interest
nodes.rationale: THE headline finding. The Destiny spec publishes fund guarantees and commissions side by side: Option 1 guarantees 2% and pays 5% year-1 commission; Option 3 guarantees 0% and pays 12%. The agent earns 2.4x more first-year commission for placing a client in a fund with a LOWER guaranteed minimum. This is a quantified incentive to move clients into weaker guarantees INSIDE A SINGLE PRODUCT LINE — no longer a hypothetical about whole life vs term. It is the commission firewall's justification stated in the vendor's own numbers. Verified: from Tatil's own published spec.

nodes.label: Commission Firewall
nodes.rationale: Architectural principle: the recommendation engine must not see commission data. Justified in this document by two vendor-published facts: (1) the Destiny conflict — 2.4x commission for a weaker guarantee; (2) Whole Life's shorter pay period halving first-year commission (30% at 10-14yr vs 60% at life/25-30yr), so the agent is paid LEAST for the limited-pay structure that often suits the client best. 'The firewall is not optional.' Counter-example worth surfacing: the annual-vs-monthly alignment, where client and agent interests genuinely coincide.

nodes.label: 200 Basis Point Investment Margin Spread
nodes.rationale: Verbatim: interest 'credited based on historic performance of the notional fund... net of a predetermined investment margin spread of 200 basis points. The investment margin spread would cover all administrative and commission expenses.' The client pays a 2% annual spread and that spread is what funds the commission. Consequence worth stating plainly: on Option 3 (0% guarantee), a year returning under 2% gross credits zero.

nodes.label: Destiny Surrender Charge Schedule (80/60/40/20/10/5)
nodes.rationale: Policy years 1-6+: 80% / 60% / 40% / 20% / 10% / 5%. Spec adds: 'Net proceeds for approved deferred annuities would be subject to any taxes applicable at time of surrender.' The compounding is the point — surrender a Registered Destiny in year 1 and you lose 80% to the charge, then 25% tax on the remainder, recovering roughly 15% of the accumulation. Described as the single most important disclosure in the product; belongs in the suitability record. A first-class lapse risk.

nodes.label: Registered (BIR) vs Unregistered Variant Decision
nodes.rationale: 'The real engine rule is: Registered vs Unregistered is the decision that determines tax treatment, not maturity age.' Registered = BIR-approved, qualifies for the TT$60k deduction and the s.8(1)(ta) / Finance Act 2026 exemption, but forbids partial withdrawals and caps maturity at 70. Unregistered may mature at 75/80/85 and allows withdrawals up to 90% of cash value, but never qualified for s.8(1)(ta) anyway.

nodes.label: 25% Tax-Free Lump Sum at Maturity
nodes.rationale: Registered Destiny: max 25% of accumulation may be taken as a TAX-FREE lump sum; the remainder becomes a 'Reduced Pension'. Small-annuity commutation: if the monthly annuity is under $500 (Registered) or under $3,000 (Unregistered), the whole accumulation may be taken as a lump sum.

nodes.label: Schedule of Guaranteed Annuity Rates
nodes.rationale: At maturity, an annuity for life is paid at the Schedule of Guaranteed Annuity Rates OR current rates if greater — a genuine floor, worth surfacing to clients rather than leaving buried.

nodes.label: Guaranteed Periods 5/10/15 Years
nodes.rationale: Shared mechanic across Destiny maturity annuities and SPIA. Options 5 / 10 / 15 years; Destiny default = 10-year unless the policyholder elects otherwise at least 1 month before maturity — a default that silently decides for most clients.

nodes.label: Spousal Benefit
nodes.rationale: Destiny: 50% or 100% of the monthly annuity, payable after the guaranteed period expires. SPIA offers a richer set: 50%, 60%, 66-2/3%, or 100%.

nodes.label: Platinum Edge
nodes.rationale: CORRECTION to earlier work: verbatim spec says Platinum Edge is 'registered as an unapproved deferred annuity with an embedded Accidental Death Benefit' — it is NOT the permanent-life product previously inferred from its 0.5% commission. That inference was wrong; the low commission makes sense once you see it is a single-deposit accumulation account. No underwriting; issue ages 1-99 (age next). Deposits: initial min $50,000 max $1,000,000; additional min $1,000 max $1,000,000/yr. NO expense charges ('the company reserves the right to introduce such charges in the future following prior notice'). Withdrawals min $5,000, must leave >=$5,000, max 1 per policy year. Death benefit = net accumulation + Accidental Death Benefit; maturity = net accumulation. Net accumulation formula: initial deposit - withdrawals/charges + additional deposits - expense charges + interest. Verified from Tatil spec.

nodes.label: Platinum Edge 2.5% Guaranteed Interest Floor
nodes.rationale: Verbatim: 'In no event will the rate of interest be less than 2.5% per annum, and once interest has been credited, the net accumulation is guaranteed.' Interest is credited annually, company-determined, with a ratchet — credited interest locks in. The 2.5% floor BEATS every Destiny option (2% / 1% / 0%). But Platinum Edge is unapproved, so it forfeits the TT$60k deduction and the s.8(1)(ta) / Finance Act 2026 exemption. That is the real, non-obvious planning trade-off the engine can surface: guaranteed rate vs tax treatment. No US tool has this comparison.

nodes.label: SPIA — Single Premium Immediate Annuity
nodes.rationale: New product, not in the commission schedule. Single premium -> immediate monthly pension; min premium $50,000. Issue ages (age next): min 51 standard / 31 ill-health; max 71 Registered / 91 Non-Registered. The ill-health minimum of 31 implies impaired-life annuity underwriting — a real planning tool for a client with reduced life expectancy. No underwriting requirements. CANNOT be surrendered in whole or in part; no loans — irreversible, which is the strongest possible reason for an affordability check before sale. Guaranteed periods 5/10/15. Spousal benefit 50/60/66-2/3/100%. Commission: Tatil agents 1.5%, Brokers 0.5%, Direct Sales 0.0%. This is the decumulation product. Verified from Tatil spec.

nodes.label: Destiny -> SPIA Retirement Arc (Accumulation to Decumulation)
nodes.rationale: Destiny is the accumulation vehicle (UL fund, no insurance); SPIA is the decumulation product that converts a Destiny maturity — or any lump sum — into lifetime income. 'Destiny -> SPIA is the complete retirement arc, and the engine should model it as such.' The 25% tax-free lump sum and the guaranteed annuity rate floor sit at the hinge between the two.
nodes.norm_label: destiny -> spia retirement arc (accumulation to decumulation)

nodes.label: Whole Life Shorter-Pay-Period Commission Penalty
nodes.rationale: First-year commission by premium-paying duration: 60% (Life; 25-30yr), 50% (20-24yr), 40% (15-19yr), 30% (10-14yr). Years 2/3/4-10/11+ are flat at 15%/10%/5%/2.5% regardless. A shorter pay period HALVES the first-year commission, so the agent is paid least for the limited-pay structure that often suits the client best — premiums retired before retirement. Another firewall justification, structurally the same shape as the Destiny conflict.

nodes.label: Agency Overrides (12% manager first-year)
nodes.rationale: Managers: 12% first-year override of Annualized Premium Income for directly supervised agents; 5% for agents under a supervisor; 10% renewal override. Supervisors: 12% first-year, 10% renewal. The load-bearing quote: 'It is noted that 85% of agents report directly to a Manager. This has been reflected in the pricing of the products.' The agency hierarchy is priced INTO the product — which is why the buyer of this app is the agency, not the individual agent. Endowment 2024 carries its own bonus/override scheme: 15% per premium in year 1, then 10% per commission year 2+.

nodes.label: Rest Assured 2024 (Final Expense)
nodes.rationale: Coverage for life, paid-up at 100, and the coverage amount is payable at age 100 if active. No underwriting. Coverage min $30,000, max $150,000 — and the $150,000 cap is AGGREGATE across all the insured's policies (a hard engine constraint, not a per-policy limit). Plans/issue ages: Pay to 60 (20-50), to 65 (20-55), to 85 (20-75), to 100 (20-80). Gender distinct; NOT smoker distinct. No policy fee. NO cash value at all — no loans, no APL, no surrender, no reduced paid-up, which removes every mechanic that Whole Life and Endowment share. Commission 30%/15%/2.5%+. Reinstatement 6 months only, versus 3 years for Whole Life. Verified from Tatil spec.

nodes.label: Graded Death Benefit (yr1 ROP / yr2 25% / yr3 100%)
nodes.rationale: Rest Assured schedule, exactly specified: year 1 = return of premiums only; year 2 = max of (25% of sum assured, return of premiums); year 3+ = 100% of sum assured. Accidental death pays the full sum insured at any duration. Confirms the knowledge-base rule with real numbers: never present Rest Assured as first-day full cover — the engine must show the graded schedule.
nodes.norm_label: graded death benefit (yr1 rop / yr2 25% / yr3 100%)

nodes.label: Endowment 2024 (ENDXX6)
nodes.rationale: Non-participating. Terms 15/20/25/30 years (durational only). Issue ages: min 1 for all; max 70 (15yr) / 65 (20yr) / 60 (25yr) / 55 (30yr) — max issue age steps down with term so every plan matures by ~85. Minimum coverage: greater of $55,000 or the amount supporting the minimum premium. Policy fee $360/yr, added to the annual premium BEFORE modal factors are applied. Minimum premium $154.44/mo, $465.30/qtr, $922.50/half, $1,800/yr, all payable in advance. Explicit premium formula: Base Premium = (Premium Rate x Face Amount x Underwriting Rating) + Policy Fee; Modal Premium = Base Premium x Modal Factor; Staff Premium = (1 - Discount Rate) x Modal Premium; Rider Premium = Benefit Rate per thousand x Coverage Amount / 1,000. Commission 50%/15%/15%/5%/5%/2.5%+. Additional rule beyond Whole Life: 'If at any time the total indebtedness equals or exceeds the gross cash value, the policy will immediately lapse.' Verified from Tatil spec.

nodes.label: Modal Factors (0.08580 / 0.25850 / 0.51250 / 1.0)
nodes.rationale: IDENTICAL across Whole Life, Endowment and Rest Assured. Monthly 0.08580 (x12 = 1.0296, +2.96%); Quarterly 0.25850 (x4 = 1.0340, +3.40%); Semi-annual 0.51250 (x2 = 1.0250, +2.50%); Annual 1.00000 (baseline). Paying monthly costs the client ~3% more than paying annually.

nodes.label: Annual-vs-Monthly Alignment (the honest recommendation)
nodes.rationale: Two facts that point the same way: monthly costs the client ~3% more than annual (modal factors), AND 'policies with annual payment modes attract an additional 5% commissions in the first year only.' So annual payment is cheaper for the client AND pays the agent more — a rare genuine alignment of interests, and a concrete honest recommendation the engine can make with no conflict whatsoever. The mirror image of the Destiny conflict; worth surfacing prominently precisely because it is the counter-example that shows the firewall is not anti-agent.

nodes.label: Policy Loans (90% of net cash value at 10%)
nodes.rationale: Universal rule across Whole Life and Endowment: loans need positive net cash value plus 3 full years of premiums; max 90% of Net Cash Value; 10% interest, changeable at will. Rest Assured has no cash value so no loans are available at all.
nodes.norm_label: policy loans (90% of net cash value at 10%)

nodes.label: Automatic Premium Loan (APL)
nodes.rationale: Premium unpaid 30 days + positive net cash value -> the premium is charged as a loan at 10%. If cash value is insufficient, coverage pro-rates and the policy LAPSES. This is the quiet mechanism by which a policy erodes itself before the client notices — directly relevant to the silently-lapsing legacy UL problem.

nodes.label: Lapse at 62 Days (notice at 31)
nodes.rationale: Universal across products: lapse processed 62 days after the due date, notice at 31 days. Reinstatement within 3 years with underwriting approval (Whole Life/Endowment) but only 6 months for Rest Assured.

nodes.label: Reduced Paid-Up ($2,000 minimum)
nodes.rationale: Available after 3 years with positive net cash value; minimum reduced coverage $2,000. Not available on Rest Assured (no cash value).

nodes.label: ANSA McAL 10% Staff Discount
nodes.rationale: 10% staff discount for the ANSA McAL group, applied universally. Enters the Endowment premium formula as: Staff Premium = (1 - Discount Rate) x Modal Premium. 'Age Next' is used for all issue ages across products.

nodes.label: GoldSpoon / GoldSpoon Gift
nodes.rationale: UNVERIFIED — child/gift plan, spec dated 2008, scanned PDF NOT YET READ. Confirmed to exist beyond the commission schedule but no mechanics extracted.

nodes.label: Corporate Destiny
nodes.rationale: Corporate registered annuity — the Corporate variant of Destiny, and Registered-only (there is no unregistered corporate option). Minimum corporate lump sum $1,000 vs $500 individual. PARTIALLY VERIFIED: only a brochure (jpg) exists in the folder, no full spec.

nodes.label: LifeSpan / LifeSpan Lite
nodes.rationale: UNVERIFIED — critical-illness-oriented product marketed on tatil.co.tt ('heart surgery... critical illness costs') with an instant-quote flow, but NO spec document exists in the Product Training and Specifications folder. Only source is the public website.

nodes.label: Policy X-ray
nodes.rationale: The engine feature that inspects existing client policies. Named here as the consumer of legacy UL knowledge: it is what will find Cashbuilder II/III on client books, and it cannot correctly evaluate them until their COI tables and crediting rates are OCR'd.

nodes.label: AM Best Rating of Tatil
nodes.rationale: AM Best affirms credit ratings of Trinidad and Tobago Insurance Limited. Noted as a real trust asset for the CLICO-scarred T&T market (project item #9) — third-party solvency validation matters more here than in markets without a collapse in living memory.

nodes.label: Three Corrections to Earlier Work
nodes.rationale: This document explicitly corrects three earlier conclusions, each traceable to reading the vendor's own spec rather than inferring from marketing or commission data: (1) Platinum Edge is an unapproved deferred annuity, NOT a permanent life product — the inference from its 0.5% commission was wrong; (2) Destiny is UL with no insurance component — the product knowledge base's 'deferred annuity with fund options' is right in effect but understates that the chassis is UL; (3) the 'warn if maturity > 70' rule is inapplicable to Registered Destiny, which only offers 50-70, and must be rewritten as a Registered-vs-Unregistered decision. Methodological lesson: inference from commission structure produced a wrong product classification.

nodes.label: Product Knowledge Base (product-knowledge-base.md)
nodes.rationale: The earlier, US/generic-derived product document that this spec extraction supersedes for anything Tatil-specific. Still the source of the UL lapse-risk framing that motivates OCR'ing Cashbuilder II/III, and the source of the graded-benefit rule that Rest Assured's schedule confirms with real numbers.

nodes.label: Central Bank of Trinidad & Tobago (CBTT)
nodes.rationale: CONFIRMED in writing from Tatil's own disclaimer: 'Tatil Life Assurance Limited… is a licensed financial institution regulated by the Central Bank of Trinidad & Tobago (CBTT). All of our Agents and Sales Representatives are registered with the CBTT and are only authorised to sell Tatil Life products.' Confirms all three: Central Bank regulation (not TTSEC), mandatory agent registration, and single-carrier tied distribution. CBTT capital adequacy regulations name universal life as a distinct policy class — regulatory proof UL is sold locally. The CBTT payment-services perimeter (money transfer, payment instruments, clearing/settlement, e-money, wallets, remittances) does NOT enumerate read-only data aggregation — a product that never moves money is likely outside PSP registration (argument from omission; confirm with counsel).

nodes.label: Household
nodes.rationale: ROOT AGGREGATE. Models the people who depend on the client, their relationships, obligations, income, and ages. Supports MULTI-GENERATIONAL AND INFORMAL DEPENDENTS (elderly parents, outside children, supported relatives overseas) — NOT A NUCLEAR COUPLE. Interface: a Household value object, built incrementally by the fact-find. Depends on NOTHING (pure). The informal-dependent model is VALIDATED by Guardian's existing parents-surgery question — 'we are making an existing, awkwardly-worded question structural, not inventing a need'.

nodes.label: PolicyLedger
nodes.rationale: Holds the client's in-force and lapsed policies — insurer, product, cover, premium, riders, cash value, beneficiary, status. Interface: PolicyLedger.add(Policy), .inForceCover(), .byInsurer(). Depends on NOTHING — populated by manual entry OR AI ingestion, AND IT DOESN'T CARE WHICH. That indifference is what keeps AI at the edges.

nodes.label: NeedsEngine
nodes.rationale: Household → NeedsProfile. T&T-localized. Interface: PURE FUNCTION computeNeeds(household, params) → NeedsProfile. Depends on ParameterTables — INJECTED, NEVER IMPORTED. The formula is NOT INVENTED; it is Tatil's standardized T&T instrument. Nets NIB survivors' benefits. Correctly OMITS the US estate-tax liquidity driver. MUST model NIS ⊕ SCP JOINTLY (a correctness fix, not an enhancement, with a cliff-edge guard at 2,500/3,500/4,500/5,500). Supports BOTH methodologies shown side by side (Tatil bottom-up headline, PALIG top-down net-worth cross-check). Consumes per-debt years-to-payoff as the ladder's decline schedule. Tested by golden-file tests against hand-computed T&T cases (NIB survivor offsets, funeral, education, mortgage; assert no estate-tax driver).

nodes.label: GapCalculator
nodes.rationale: NeedsProfile − PolicyLedger.inForceCover() → Gap. 'TRIVIAL CODE; IT IS THE MONEY SHOT OF THE WHOLE PRODUCT.' Depends on NeedsEngine and PolicyLedger. Must zero group cover from age 70 per the group-life lapse rule.

nodes.label: ProductCatalog
nodes.rationale: Structured store of T&T life products — insurer, product type, rate tables (age/sex/smoker/band), riders, underwriting rules, non-medical limits, exclusions, and a STATUS FIELD (new/legacy) so the X-ray can identify old products like Cashbuilder on a client's book. Interface: RateProvider — quote(product, applicant, coverAmount) → Premium | NoRates (the NoRates arm is what makes 'no silent truncation' possible). Depends on rate data (EXTERNAL — the spec's biggest risk, downgraded to Medium once the founder was identified as the rate-book source). Real T&T taxonomy from the Tatil catalog: term (convertible level 10/15/20/25, term-to-age 60/65/70) · permanent (whole life, limited-pay) · accumulation (endowment 15–30 yr, fund-linked deferred annuity, Publicsaver hybrids) · specialist (final expense/simplified issue, riders) · group (group life, group annuity, deposit administration). Convertibility is a MODELLED ATTRIBUTE; carrier conversion windows must come from here, never assumed.

nodes.label: RecommendationEngine
nodes.rationale: (Gap, Budget, Catalog, Constraints) → [Package × 3] + Rationale. CONSTRAINED OPTIMIZATION over a policy ladder: term laddering against declining obligation, a whole-life floor for permanent need, CI riders. Maximize coverage adequacy subject to totalMonthlyPremium ≤ budget. EMITS EXACTLY THREE DIFFERENTIATED OPTIONS, NOT ONE (Guardian's Decision Meeting agenda) — meaningfully differentiated (maximum cover / balanced / lowest premium) with DISTINCT rationale, not three cosmetic variants. Reasons from the VERIFIED product knowledge base — matching rules per product type, NOT AD-HOC LOGIC. Budget elicited as a % band, normalized to monthly TTD internally; all product rates normalize to monthly before optimization regardless of the carrier's native billing frequency. Interface: PURE FUNCTION. DETERMINISTIC AND REPRODUCIBLE — same inputs produce BYTE-IDENTICAL output, always. 'THAT PROPERTY IS AUDITABILITY.' 🔴 COMMISSION IS NEVER AN INPUT. Depends on ProductCatalog (via RateProvider) and GapCalculator. Property-tested: never exceeds budget; never recommends an ineligible product; always produces a rationale; NEVER SILENTLY DROPS A PRODUCT.

nodes.label: CommissionCalculator
nodes.rationale: AGENT-FACING, STRICTLY DOWNSTREAM. Given a recommendation ALREADY FIXED, computes the agent's expected commission from the carrier schedule (heaped first-year + renewal trail; e.g. Tatil Whole Life 60/15/10/5/5/2.5, Destiny annuity 5/3/1 + trail). Depends on a FIXED recommendation + the carrier commission schedule. NEVER SITS UPSTREAM OF RecommendationEngine — 'the two never touch'.

nodes.label: SuitabilityRecord
nodes.rationale: The Market Conduct artifact — inputs, rules fired, alternatives considered, rejection reasons, rates-as-of date, catalog version. KEY DESIGN: EMITTED BY RecommendationEngine, NOT BUILT SEPARATELY — 'compliance FALLS OUT of the recommendation FOR FREE' (idea #3, free). Modeled on Tatil's existing attestation, signed and dated by BOTH client and agent, which BUNDLES suitability + affordability — consequently affordability (#5) cannot be deferred; v1 must capture monthly income and expense (fact-find Q2) and assert premium sustainability. Can affirmatively state the recommendation was made WITHOUT REFERENCE TO COMMISSION. Depends on RecommendationEngine.

nodes.label: ParameterTables
nodes.rationale: Year-indexed, DATED, SOURCED T&T constants; seeded from the T-T-Financial-Insurance-Hub repo. Every value carries a verification status from the July 2026 audit — DO NOT ENCODE AN UNVERIFIED VALUE WITHOUT A FLAG. ✅ VERIFIED 3–0: Health Surcharge (8.25/wk above 469.99/mo else 4.80) · Health Surcharge exemptions (under 16 · 60 and over · pension-only income — MATERIAL: never charge a 62-year-old) · TT$60,000 cap · NIS 16.2% eff. 2026-01-05 (⅓ ee / ⅔ er) · 16 classes & 13,600+/mo ceiling · pension formula structure · 750-contribution threshold · minimum pension 3,000 · Retirement Grant 3× monetary value min 3,000 · retirement age 60→65, +1yr/2yrs from Jan 2028, reaching 65 in 2036. ✅ TRANSCRIPT-SOURCED: averaging basis is WHOLE WORKING LIFE — not final salary, not last 7 years; qualifying conditions 150 contributions incl. 50 in last 3 yrs OR employed 5 of last 7 yrs AND 750 for a pension (the '7 years' is an ELIGIBILITY GATE, not the averaging window); 750 may include paid, Voluntary, Age Credits, Benefit Credits; claiming at 60–64 requires CEASING insurable employment, at 65 paid regardless; earnings above 13,600/mo contribute at Class XVI but DO NOT INCREASE THE PENSION. 🔴 BLOCKING: PENSION_RATES is OUTDATED — the repo holds the stale 2008 table. 🔴 UNRESOLVED: 2016 increment values unpublished — DO NOT GUESS. 🟡 PROVISIONAL (2–1): 19.2% from Jan 2027 — budget announcement + arithmetic (16.2+3), NO GAZETTED SCHEDULE EXISTS; never show 2027 figures as settled. 🟡 Finance Bill 2026 exemption — a BILL, not an Act; code conditional on assent. ⚪ UNVERIFIED: personal allowance 90,000/yr and PAYE bands (25% ≤1M, 30% >1M) — negative evidence only; 70% NIS deductibility — ENTIRELY unverified. ✅ SOURCE-SCRAPED: SCP means-test bands, SCP age/residency, NIS pension counts as SCP assessed income (grant excluded). ✅ MARKET-STANDARD: benchmark allocation. Migration action: port the table structure; refresh contribution tables to 2026; REPLACE benefit rates with the 2016 schedule; add 2027 as PROVISIONAL; add Health Surcharge exemptions; add the Finance Bill 2026 exemption gated on assent. Also required: Section 134(6) and public servants' pension + gratuity (unverified; lead: Finance Bill 2026 cll. 4–5).

nodes.label: PENSION_RATES Stale-Table Defect
nodes.rationale: 🔴 BLOCKING. NIBTT publishes retirement/invalidity benefit rates IN TWO PLACES WITH DIFFERENT VALUES AND DOES NOT RECONCILE THEM: the Benefits section serves a STALE 2008 table (335.83 … 2,475.70 — what the repo holds, and what NIBTT's own Retirement pages link to), while the CURRENT 2016 table (eff. 2016-09-05, Class I 566.72 … Class XVI 4,079.40) sits under /Contribution_Rates/. Current values are ~69% higher. THE FAILURE MODE: understated NIS → OVERSTATED GAP → RECOMMENDS MORE PRODUCT — a real MIS-SELLING EXPOSURE on a SIGNED suitability record. 🔴 TWO OPPOSITE WRONG ANSWERS WERE GIVEN: first a verification round claimed 3–0 the rates were '18 years obsolete, understating pensions by ~40%' and supplied replacement figures that 'appear nowhere on NIBTT' — it had carried the 2016 CONTRIBUTION-table date onto the BENEFIT table and fabricated values to match; had it been actioned it would have WRITTEN A REAL MIS-SELLING BUG INTO THE ENGINE. Then the same figures were called a fabrication after scraping ONE page — and the founder's pointer to the rates section found them EXACTLY AS REPORTED. RULES DERIVED: scrape the issuer's own page before 'verifying' a published number; A UNANIMOUS VOTE IS NOT TRUTH; SCRAPING IS NOT VERIFICATION EITHER — one page is a sample; when a number is disputed, find EVERY page the issuer publishes it on and reconcile, because AGENCIES CONTRADICT THEMSELVES and NIBTT demonstrably does; when verification contradicts a practitioner, GO TO SOURCE BEFORE OVERRIDING THEM. Every single-page 'confirmed from source' claim in this project — INCLUDING THE SCP BANDS — needs a second source. ⚠️ Do not encode the 'NIS Stuff' markdown files: three of them give three different answers for the same figure (Class XVI: $6,799 vs $5,500 vs '$10–12k estimated'), none matching the repo or the verified schedule; their '50% of assumed average weekly earnings' method is an INFERENCE (its own text says the pension 'appears to be approximately 50%') whereas the transcript describes a LOOKUP TABLE of basic rates + increments. Authoritative chain: published dated NIBTT benefit schedule → basic + increments → lifetime-average class lookup.

nodes.label: NIS Was Never Designed to Fund a Middle-Class Retirement
nodes.rationale: 🔴 'THE STRONGEST CLIENT-FACING INSIGHT IN THE PROJECT.' The 3,000 minimum is THE DOMINANT RULE, NOT A FLOOR: every basic rate in the (2008) table, all sixteen classes, is BELOW 3,000/month (top class 2,475.70). A retiree exceeds 3,000 ONLY VIA INCREMENTS — and a Class XVI TOP EARNER needs ~1,050 contributions (~20 years) JUST TO BEAT THE FLOOR that a Class I retiree gets at 750. Combined with the 13,600/mo insurable CEILING and WHOLE-LIFE AVERAGING, three public NIBTT facts prove NIS was never designed to fund a middle-class retirement — HONESTLY, FROM THE ISSUER'S OWN TABLE, WITH NO SALES FRAMING. Raises the stakes on SCP: if most retirees land at exactly 3,000 that sits squarely in the 2,501–3,500 SCP band. ⚠️ PARTIALLY SUPERSEDED: this reasoning rests on the STALE 2008 basics; under the 2016 table the minimum binds only for Classes I–XII (XIII–XVI exceed 3,000 on basics alone), and the 'every class is below the minimum' claim is explicitly STRUCK as an artifact of the stale values.
nodes.norm_label: nis was never designed to fund a middle-class retirement

nodes.label: AIIngestionService
nodes.rationale: Document → structured Policy. 'AN ACCELERANT, NEVER A DEPENDENCY.' Structured MANUAL ENTRY is the PRIMARY path (~90 seconds per policy). Output is ALWAYS AGENT-CONFIRMED before entering the ledger. Tested: AI output must always route through agent confirmation; UNCONFIRMED EXTRACTIONS MUST NEVER REACH THE LEDGER. Risk note: OCR of heterogeneous policy documents is hard (Medium) — OCR is added AFTER seeing real documents; the MVP does not bet on it.

nodes.label: AIExplanationService
nodes.rationale: Engine output → plain language for the portal and the suitability narrative. 'NEVER DECIDES ANYTHING.'

nodes.label: ClientPortal
nodes.rationale: Read view: household, policies, need, gap, proposed package. 'THE CLIENT PORTAL'S JOB IS THE GAP BETWEEN THE MEETINGS' — not a nice-to-have, its STRUCTURAL purpose, and why the agent-led marketplace model is right. 'The portal is the continuous line; meetings are punctuation.' The client's phone becomes the true second screen via the portal, BUT THE MVP MUST NOT DEPEND ON THAT BEING PRESENT IN THE ROOM.

nodes.label: PresentationMode
nodes.rationale: A CLIENT-SAFE RENDER of the agent's live session. Same data, different view. Explicit toggle. Mirrors eMoney's Decision Center Presentation View (2025 redesign). THE OBLIGATION COUNTER DUAL VIEW: agent sees it live; client sees it on reveal. Two mechanics make this LEGITIMATE RATHER THAN SNEAKY, and BOTH ARE REQUIRED: (1) presentation mode is A HARD TOGGLE, NOT A HOPE — same session, client-safe render, entered deliberately; (2) THE AGENT'S NUMBER STAYS QUIET — a small glanceable figure in a status bar, NOT a banner. In T&T agent and client are frequently at ONE KITCHEN TABLE looking at ONE LAPTOP. If the client catches the number they must see A PRACTITIONER'S INSTRUMENT PANEL, NOT A CONCEALED SALES GAUGE. 'In a market still carrying the CLICO wound, getting this wrong doesn't cost a sale — IT COSTS TRUST.' Also mitigates the risk of a client under-reporting dependents to game the counter.

nodes.label: AI at the Edges, Deterministic Core
nodes.rationale: THE ORGANIZING PRINCIPLE: AI ingestion (documents in) → [DETERMINISTIC CORE — decides everything] → AI explanation (plain language out). TEST OF CORRECTNESS: IF BOTH AI SERVICES FAIL, THE PRODUCT STILL WORKS AND STILL RECOMMENDS CORRECTLY — it is merely less convenient. IF THAT CEASES TO BE TRUE, THE ARCHITECTURE HAS BEEN VIOLATED. WHY NON-NEGOTIABLE: TTSEC's 2018 robo-advice paper lists 'review of algorithms and methodologies' as a regulatory focus area, and the Central Bank's Market Conduct Guideline imposes parallel suitability duties. 'THE MODEL DECIDED' IS NOT AN AUDITABLE METHODOLOGY. AN LLM THAT HALLUCINATES A COVER AMOUNT IS NOT A BUG — IT IS A MIS-SELLING EVENT. Enforced by a determinism test: identical inputs run twice, diff the output, MUST BE BYTE-IDENTICAL.
nodes.norm_label: ai at the edges, deterministic core

nodes.label: Agent as Recommender of Record
nodes.rationale: THE REGISTERED AGENT IS ALWAYS THE RECOMMENDER OF RECORD. 'SOFTWARE PROPOSES; THE AGENT DISPOSES.' The agent's review/adjust/approve step in Meeting 2 is 'THE REGULATORY HINGE' — it keeps the vendor OUT of the intermediary perimeter. NOT OPTIONAL, NOT SKIPPABLE. Note 'insurance consultants' are themselves a registered category under the Insurance Act — the vendor must not act as one. Every recommendation carries provenance: rates as of date, source, catalog version, rules fired, alternatives rejected and why. Legal review required before launch on the investment-linked boundary and whether the software constitutes intermediary activity.

nodes.label: No Silent Truncation
nodes.rationale: If the optimizer COULDN'T EVALUATE a product (missing rates), it SAYS SO: 'cannot evaluate product X — no rates'. 'Silently omitting READS AS we considered everything WHEN WE DIDN'T — the exact mis-selling failure mode.' Enabled by the RateProvider's NoRates return arm. Also forbids omitting the cheaper term that works, making it the mechanism behind the anti-mis-selling guardrail. Property-tested: never silently drops a product.

nodes.label: The Policy X-ray Wedge
nodes.rationale: WEDGE DECISION: Policy X-ray first. 'The ONLY wedge that pays BOTH SIDES ON DAY ONE; builds the data asset everything else needs; UNCOPYABLE BY INCUMBENTS.' It slots into an EXISTING RITUAL — agents ALREADY end Meeting 1 with 'here's what to bring', so 'our wedge doesn't create a new behaviour, IT INSTRUMENTS ONE THAT EXISTS.' It is fact-find question 4 ('What do you already have?'). It is what finds legacy Cashbuilder ULs heading for silent lapse. And it survives where bank-statement import doesn't: 'getting statements from clients is a hard trust ask; THE POLICY ASK SURVIVES BECAUSE AGENTS ALREADY COLLECT EXACTLY THAT DATA.'

nodes.label: Conversation Drives, Canvas Reflects
nodes.rationale: The fact-find is 'the most-hated moment in insurance sales'. THE BAR: eMoney's answer is a dense form taking 3–6 months to master that its own 5-star reviewers call 'kind of clunky'; RightCapital beats it on EASE, NOT POWER. THE PATTERN: triage first, then ONE CALM QUESTION AT A TIME (never a scrollable form) while the HOUSEHOLD CANVAS grows beside it. 'The conversation does the input; the canvas holds the context.' On mobile the canvas collapses to a ribbon of faces with the running total pinned right. REQUIREMENTS, NOT POLISH: never more than one question on screen (no form to dread) · five questions, not twelve (honest progress; depth comes later, once the client is invested) · EVERYTHING SKIPPABLE ('That's everyone →' always available; NO RED VALIDATION ERRORS MID-FLOW) · PERMISSION LANGUAGE ('It doesn't have to be official' — the line that lets someone name an outside child or a supported nephew; the household model earning its place in the UI) · VISIBLE ACCOMPLISHMENT (the canvas grows; THEY'RE BUILDING, NOT BEING AUDITED).

nodes.label: Depth in the Engine, Not the Interface
nodes.rationale: THE TEST FOR ANY NEW DOMAIN DISCOVERY: DOES IT ADD A QUESTION, OR AN INSIGHT? IF IT ADDS A QUESTION, IT FAILED. Everything the research surfaced — 16 NIS classes, four SCP cliffs, Health Surcharge, PAYE brackets, 70% deductibility, two needs methodologies, the benchmark — is DERIVED FROM THE SAME FIVE ANSWERS, NOT ASKED. The ONLY addition is 'when did you start working?' (NIS contribution weeks), which fits the conversation rather than a form.
nodes.norm_label: depth in the engine, not the interface

nodes.label: Triage Selects the Insight (insight is rationed)
nodes.rationale: 'INSIGHT IS RATIONED, NOT DASHBOARDED. We have three strong revelations and SHOWING ALL THREE IS HOW THIS BECOMES OVERBEARING. TRIAGE SELECTS WHICH ONE YOU GET: retirement → the SCP clawback · my family → the canvas and the gap · debt → the leak. ONE JOURNEY, ONE HEADLINE.' Triage is also the architecture that routes between Tatil's four needs — 'so the architecture doesn't change when 3 and 4 arrive'.
nodes.norm_label: triage selects the insight (insight is rationed)

nodes.label: Data Protection Act 2011 s.6(l) Hosting Constraint
nodes.rationale: Only Part I (ss.1–6) of the T&T Data Protection Act 2011 is PROCLAIMED. But S.6(l) IS LIVE TODAY: personal information disclosed OUTSIDE T&T may only go to jurisdictions with COMPARABLE SAFEGUARDS. This constrains cloud hosting — EU/UK (GDPR) reads as comfortably comparable; US-ONLY IS A HARDER ARGUMENT. Build to the UNPROCLAIMED Part IV anyway: s.69 would capture this product EVEN IF HOSTED ABROAD, and 'proclamation is a switch someone can flip'. Legal review required before launch.
nodes.norm_label: data protection act 2011 s.6(l) hosting constraint

nodes.label: First Milestone: One Household, One Carrier, Three Products
nodes.rationale: One household, one carrier, three products, END TO END — INCLUDING THE PORTAL. NOT: any subsystem built to completion. 'The VERTICAL SLICE proves the architecture, the regulatory posture, and the both-sides value proposition SIMULTANEOUSLY — and it's the smallest thing an agency can actually look at and buy.' A vertical slice OVER completed subsystems.
nodes.norm_label: first milestone: one household, one carrier, three products

nodes.label: Annuities Are In Scope (life licence finding)
nodes.rationale: IN T&T, ANNUITIES FALL UNDER THE LIFE LICENCE — a CBTT-registered life agent is licensed to sell them, and NO TTSEC REGISTRATION IS INVOLVED. SOURCE: the founder, a CBTT-registered agent of 13+ years. Consistent with Tatil's own disclaimer and with Round 2's finding that Securities Act 'investment advice' attaches to SECURITIES specifically. 'THIS SUPERSEDES THE EARLIER DEFERRAL, WHICH WAS BASED ON MY INFERENCE RATHER THAN PRACTITIONER KNOWLEDGE.' CONSEQUENCE: RETIREMENT BECOMES FIRST-CLASS IN V1, NOT ROADMAP — it is Tatil's Need #1, the engine substantially exists in the repo, the SCP clawback is our strongest insight, and it is the founder's deepest expertise; the triage architecture already routes to it as a distinct journey. Annuities and the TT$60k envelope (#6) are IN. STILL OUT OF V1: unit-linked / investment-linked products where an explicit securities component may attach — narrow, revisit with counsel, DO NOT LET IT RE-BLOCK ANNUITIES. ⚠️ NOTE the §7 risk table still lists 'Investment-linked products straddle two regimes / Deferred from v1 / Legal review before adding annuities, UL, endowment' — an internal tension with this finding.
nodes.norm_label: annuities are in scope (life licence finding)

nodes.label: Original Build, Not a Clone
nodes.rationale: THE LEGAL BOUNDARY: functional understanding only — NO CODE OR PIXEL-EXACT DESIGN COPYING of eMoney. 'Explicitly not doing: copying eMoney code or exact UI.' THE MOAT: the DOMAIN LAYER (T&T tax, NIB, household structure, insurance products) is ORIGINAL. The research report echoes it: 'Findings support functional understanding only. Copying eMoney's code or pixel-exact designs is off the table. TTSEC/tax conclusions are research, not legal advice.'

nodes.label: Agent-Led Marketplace (buyer decision)
nodes.rationale: BUYER: agent pays, client gets portal — 'proven (eMoney's model); matches how the market already works'. SEGMENT: TIED AGENTS FIRST, brokers later — 'largest population; comparison features stay BEHIND A FLAG so we don't offend the first buyer'. Risk: agency gatekeeps tied agents (Medium) — mitigated because 'THE AGENCY IS THE BUYER, NOT AN OBSTACLE: compliance + persistency + ramp is the agency pitch'.

nodes.label: Tatil Quotation Rate Grid (192 quotes)
nodes.rationale: AUTHORITATIVE. Extracted from Tatil's own quotation system: 192 PDFs, 192 parsed, 0 errors. Systematic 3 products x 2 sexes x 2 smoker statuses x 4 issue ages (25/35/45/55) x 4 sums insured ($100k/$250k/$500k/$750k). WL complete (64 quotes), LP65 complete (64), T65 partial (43 face-first + 21 budget-first). Founder undersold it as 'an idea of how policies are priced' - it is a real rate grid. Quote date Sep 2024: carries an effective date like every other parameter; re-verify before launch because rates change. Extracted to research/data/tatil_quotes.json and research/data/tatil_rate_grid.csv.

nodes.label: RateProvider interface
nodes.rationale: The spec interface the grid seeds. The spec assumed a thin seed of '2-3 products from an agent's rate book'; reality is a complete 4x4 grid for two products plus a partial third, seedable today from tatil_rate_grid.csv. The same interface anticipates federation - general insurance is just another provider.

nodes.label: Rate data risk (spec's #1 risk)
nodes.rationale: The spec named rate data the single High risk - 'outside our control... gates the recommendation engine entirely'. The 192-quote grid directly attacks it: DOWNGRADE High -> Medium. Residual risk is the Sep 2024 effective date and the T65 gaps, not availability.

nodes.label: Term vs Whole Life price gap (3.2x)
nodes.rationale: M/NS/35/$500k: T65 $144.77 vs WL $467.18 (3.2x) vs LP65 $549.98 (3.8x). Term pays 35% first-year commission, whole life 60%. The agent is paid 1.7x more to sell a product costing the client 3.2x more. This is the concrete number the anti-mis-selling suitability rule exists to surface - 'when term satisfies the need, term must appear among the three options with its lower cost shown'. No longer an abstraction: EXTRACTED from real quotes.
nodes.norm_label: term vs whole life price gap (3.2x)

nodes.label: Premium banding non-linearity
nodes.rationale: WL M/NS/25: $100k -> $195.20 but $750k -> $500.64. 7.5x the cover for 2.6x the premium. Policy fee plus 4 bands ($65k-150k / 150k-500k / 500k-2M / 2M+). The engine must NEVER scale premium linearly - it must look up the band. The grid is what makes that testable. T65 policy fee $30.89/month ($360/yr) matches the Whole Life and Endowment specs exactly - cross-product consistency confirmed.

nodes.label: Budget-first (#-prefixed) reverse quotes
nodes.rationale: 21 T65 PDFs prefixed '#' are reverse quotes: fix the premium at a round $150/month, solve for cover (F/NS/25 -> $594,185; M/NS/25 -> $291,283; F/NS/55 -> $193,052). This is exactly what the RecommendationEngine does - a budget anchor, then solve for maximum coverage adequacy subject to totalMonthlyPremium <= budget. The founder ALREADY works this way manually. The design isn't novel; it's automation of an existing practice - which is the safest kind of product. Strong validation of the design, not just a data point.

nodes.label: Minimum face floor ($150,000)
nodes.rationale: At M/S/55, $150/month cannot reach the $150,000 minimum face - premium goes to $207.08, over budget (M/S/45 also hits the floor at $148.99). 'Budget cannot buy the minimum' is a REAL OUTCOME the engine must handle gracefully, not an error. This is the negative-leak case from the budget design in product form.

nodes.label: Cash surrender value tables
nodes.rationale: 128 of the 192 quotes carry full CSV tables by duration (years 1-65). WL M/NS/35/$500k: $0 for years 1-3, $2,875 at year 4, $31,283 at 10, $176,804 at 30, reaching the full $500,000 at 65. Real cash-value data - enough to model whole-life accumulation without guessing.

nodes.label: Filename/content mismatch (23 files)
nodes.rationale: 23 files' filenames disagree with their contents - e.g. '#T65 - F - NS - Age 25 - $250k.pdf' actually quotes $594,185. Several '#' files with different names hold identical content. Rule: TRUST THE PDF, NEVER THE FILENAME. The extractor records filename_face, face_matches_filename and quote_type so this cannot silently corrupt the catalog. A provenance-integrity control, not a data-cleaning chore.

nodes.label: Interpolate within, refuse to extrapolate
nodes.rationale: The grid has 4 ages and 4 faces; real clients are 31 with $380k. Interpolate WITHIN the grid, REFUSE to extrapolate outside it, and flag interpolated quotes as estimates pending a real illustration. An honesty constraint on the RateProvider, and it must respect banding rather than linear interpolation on face.

nodes.label: Smoker loading (+43%)
nodes.rationale: Real and steep. WL M/45/$500k: NS $683.83 -> S $978.55 (+43%). LP65 at 55/$750k: $3,178.89 -> $4,037.32 (+27%). Confirms the spec's 'smoker distinct' rating dimension - and gives the engine a concrete, honest number for a cessation conversation.

nodes.label: Sex-distinct rates (female ~13% lower)
nodes.rationale: Female rates consistently lower: M/NS/35/$500k $467.18 vs F/NS/35/$500k $405.83 (-13%). Confirms the spec's 'sex distinct' rating dimension across the whole grid, not just one cell.

nodes.label: General_Raters_Portal
nodes.author: founder
nodes.rationale: BUILT AND WORKING. Founder-built (explicitly NOT Tatil's official corporate system) T&T/Tatil-specific motor/property/health rating and quoting with real rate tables. Full workflow already implemented: client intake -> rating engine -> manager approval -> client proposal -> official CSR forms -> pipeline management. Stack: HTML/JS/TS, Supabase (Postgres + edge functions), PWA. Rating logic in motor-rates.js/property-rates.js/health-rates.js mirrored as edge functions over 01-schema-motor-v3.sql. Its existence KILLS the 'capture, don't quote' recommendation, which rested on general rating being a scope explosion. Sibling repo TATILraters referenced but not yet examined.

nodes.label: Motor rating engine
nodes.author: founder
nodes.rationale: Real encoded rates: Private Comprehensive 0.08 of SI, Platinum Qualified 0.0195 flat net, Third-Party TT$1,700 (<2000cc)/TT$2,000 (2000cc+). NCD scales by class, loadings (age 17-24 +20%/+50%, EV/Hybrid +20%, Honda City +30%), floors (Comp min net 2.5% SI, Platinum 1.95%, min premiums $2,000/$1,150/$7,500), tax 6% exempt at 60+. UI encodes 'only 2 discounts per vehicle including NCD'. Most transactional and least connected to planning - unify rating LAST.

nodes.label: HomeSure property rating engine
nodes.author: founder
nodes.rationale: Building $3.75 per mille standard, hard floor $3.50 (discouraged), flood-prone $5.00. Contents 0.4% general / 1% electronics / jewellery at territory All Risks rate. Personal Accident $30/person (18-65). Free liability with Building or Contents: public $250,000, domestic servants $100,000. Underwriting referral triggers encoded (flood-prone, subsidence, non-concrete, catastrophe claim in 5 yrs, prior declination, business use or 40+ day vacancy). IPT 6% waived at 60+.

nodes.label: CoverCare health rating engine
nodes.author: founder
nodes.rationale: Three tiers: Base Plan (IAH6), Major Medical (5 levels $50K-$500K), Elite CoverCare (requires min monthly income TT$12,000). Age bands <40/40-49/50-59/60-65/66-67/68-70; new business entry caps at 55, standard terminates at 70, Elite extends to 75. Maternity only ages <40-49. Monthly drug allowance $800-$4,000. HEALTH FIRST if rating ever unifies, because of the CI overlap.

nodes.label: Tatil design system (teal + gold)
nodes.author: founder
nodes.rationale: PRODUCTION-PROVEN with real agents - use these tokens, do not fork the design language. Deep teal #04323C primary, gold #C8A24A accent, Source Serif 4 headings, Montserrat body. Cards white, 1px border, 14px radius, soft shadow; manager-level cards upgrade to gold borders + raised shadow as a STATUS SIGNAL, not decoration. >=44px touch targets, teal focus ring 0 0 0 3px rgba(4,50,60,.12). Signature treatment: gold caps on dark teal for key statistics. Unicode glyphs, no icon fonts, no gradients, minimal animation. Dates dd-Mmm-yyyy, money $6,240.00 TT$ implied. Content tone already matches the fact-find principles: 'an experienced agent talking to a colleague or client', precise terminology, honest specific caveats.

nodes.label: Design system convergence
nodes.rationale: The fact-find mockups independently chose teal #0E7C7B + gold #A57C1B + serif headings (Charter); the portal already used deep teal #04323C + gold #C8A24A + Source Serif 4. Converged on teal + gold + serif-headings with no coordination. A real finding, not a curiosity: the two products can share one visual identity without either being redesigned - they already look like one company's work. This is what makes federate_not_merge cheap.

nodes.label: Federate, don't merge
nodes.rationale: RECOMMENDATION: two products, one platform, one design system - and sequence them. (1) Ship the life MVP first, unchanged - harder, more defensible, more differentiated, and not done. (2) Share the substrate NOW: design tokens, Supabase schema patterns, intake->rate->approve->proposal->pipeline workflow. (3) Extend the Policy X-ray to capture general policies immediately - now cheaper because the data shapes exist; premiums feed the leak and the 5% benchmark, renewal dates are review triggers. (4) The life app reads the general portal's data for the picture; the general portal keeps its own engines. One client record, two engines - ProductCatalog/RateProvider already anticipates this. (5) Health first if unifying, motor last. TRADE-OFFS AGAINST MERGING: different sales motions (general transactional/annually renewing vs life advisory/episodic - one UI serving both risks serving neither); the MVP hasn't shipped and merging two systems before either is proven is how both die; different rate volatility and refresh cadences. FOR MERGING: the client is one person whose protection gap spans life/motor/home/health; both benchmark fact finders already table general insurance; PALIG allocates General Insurance 5%; renewal dates give a RECURRING contact reason that life planning lacks.

nodes.label: Licence perimeter (Tatil vs Tatil Life)
nodes.rationale: Tatil (general) and Tatil Life are SEPARATE COMPANIES; Tatil's own disclaimer says its agents are 'only authorised to sell Tatil Life products'. The document flagged this as the only surviving constraint and a blocking question before architecture: can a Tatil Life agent advise on and place Tatil general business, and under what registration? RESOLVED: the founder holds BOTH licences (cross-confirmed in sales-craft-library.md line 76, which notes key-person, buy-sell and group benefits are therefore all sellable). Same perimeter discipline as annuities, where the founder's practitioner knowledge settled it when desk research couldn't.

nodes.label: AgencyTrack
nodes.author: founder
nodes.rationale: A THIRD existing asset, already BUILT: sales activity tracking with a persistency recorder and career levels. That is idea #15 (book dashboard) and half of #4 (lapse prevention). Three existing systems now: planning (to build), general rating (built), agent activity (built) - the platform story is stronger than any one of them.

nodes.label: Health / Critical Illness overlap
nodes.rationale: CoverCare and LifeSPAN answer the same client fear from different angles. Modeling a health shock without knowing their health cover is modeling half the problem. This overlap is the reason health goes FIRST if rating ever unifies, and motor last.

nodes.label: Sales Craft Library
nodes.rationale: A REFERENCE LIBRARY, explicitly NOT a source of engine rules. Founder's purpose: 'just for memory to have the ability to understand the softer skills of making recommendations and to help come up with creative ideas.' Corpus: Feldman Method (100pp), High-Touch Selling/Savage (200pp), Creative Selling for the 1990's (222pp), 198 Prospecting Letters (98pp), Principal's Concept Marketing (12pp), 'Not Just for Dying Anymore' (18pp), Corporation Tax Training (52pp), Guardian OP, Maritime Sales Presentation (92pp, scanned), plus the three scanned Tolani playbooks. ACTION: do not graph as domain facts - catalog it, reference it, don't encode it. Treat Guardian OP and Maritime Sales Presentation as competitor intelligence.

nodes.label: AIExplanationService
nodes.rationale: Where the sales-craft corpus belongs: deterministic core, AI at the edges. Permitted uses - how to SAY a recommendation the engine already made; fact-find soft questions in the 'paint me a picture' register; creative feature ideation. Forbidden - NeedsEngine, RecommendationEngine, ParameterTables. Principles to carry in: ask don't tell; concept before product; make the abstract concrete (Feldman's move - already mirrored by the $1,300/month leak and the household canvas obligation counter); living benefits not death benefits; the objection is the conversation (three options generate fewer objections than accept/reject of one).

nodes.label: The Feldman Method
nodes.author: Andrew Thomson
nodes.rationale: 100pp, ~188k chars, text-extractable. Ben Feldman - the most famous life insurance salesman in history; the canonical text on needs-based selling and the 'one more sale' discipline. Feldman's signature move - turning an abstract obligation into a vivid specific number or image - is the thing the leak figure and the household canvas obligation counter already do.

nodes.label: High-Touch Selling (John Savage)
nodes.author: John Savage
nodes.rationale: 200pp, ~80k chars, text-extractable. Savage is a legendary practitioner; the book is about QUESTIONS, not pitches - directly relevant to fact-find design. 'Ask, don't tell' is already the fact-find thesis ('conversation drives, canvas reflects'), which is why the Guardian soft questions were the right instinct.

nodes.label: Principal's Concept Marketing Guide
nodes.author: Principal
nodes.rationale: 12pp - the most directly useful item in the corpus, and the only one read in full. Four-step structure maps almost exactly onto the two-meeting flow: Learn -> product knowledge base; Approach -> triage + book dashboard (#15); Consult -> Discovery meeting/fact-find; Take action -> Decision meeting/three options. ORGANIZING INSIGHT: concepts are indexed BY NEED FIRST, THEN BY PRODUCT - 'organized by some of the most common needs a business or individual has to plan for, and then focuses on a popular solution'. That is exactly Tatil's Four Basic Needs architecture, arrived at independently by a US carrier - further evidence that need-first (not product-first) is the correct information architecture, and it's what the triage already does.

nodes.label: Dr Sanjay Tolani playbooks
nodes.author: Dr Sanjay Tolani
nodes.rationale: UNEXTRACTED - all three are SCANNED, 312 pages with zero extractable text: Objection Playbook (163pp), Closing Playbook (75pp), Sales Maximizer (74pp). The most directly applicable material to the product - objection handling is exactly what the AI explanation layer needs a register for. ACTION: worth OCRing; the highest-value unextracted material in the corpus. 163 pages on objections says the sale happens AFTER the first 'no' - relevant to the three-options design.

nodes.label: Business market gap
nodes.rationale: The business market is ENTIRELY ABSENT from the spec - it was designed around individuals (household canvas, personal needs). Yet the products already exist in Tatil's book: Cashbuilder III is employer-owned deferred compensation (s.134(6A)), Corporate Destiny exists, and Group Life / Group Annuity / Deposit Administration are in the commission schedule. The founder holds both licences, so key-person, buy-sell and group benefits are all sellable. The creative move: the 'household canvas' becomes an 'ORG CANVAS' - who depends on this BUSINESS? Same mechanic and same needs formula (replace income/value, cover debt), different subject and different obligor. Worth a roadmap entry.

nodes.label: Key Person insurance
nodes.rationale: Principal's named concept: 'The most valuable asset of any business is the people who contribute most to its success... Key person insurance can provide a financial cushion with cost-effective liquidity for replacing employees who critically impact the value of the business.' A genuinely creative extension - the household canvas mechanic applied to an org. Sits alongside buy-sell, executive bonus and deferred comp as business/employer concepts.

nodes.label: Persuasion firewall
nodes.rationale: Sales craft informs HOW a recommendation is explained, NEVER WHAT is recommended. 'That is the commission firewall applied to persuasion.' The distinction matters because this corpus is PERSUASION LITERATURE - its job is to make a case; the engine's job is to be right. Keep them apart. Same structural move as the commission firewall: keep an incentive out of the decision path and confine it to the explanation layer.

nodes.label: No account aggregator covers Trinidad & Tobago
nodes.rationale: RESOLVED. Salt Edge: zero Caribbean coverage (Americas = 4 countries, 10 connections). Plaid: zero (~20 countries, North America/UK/Europe). nodes.label: Robo-advice perimeter — TTSEC requires registration
nodes.rationale: RESOLVED, and the most consequential finding of Round 2. CONFIRMED 3-0: no robo-adviser-specific rules; the investment-adviser provisions of the Securities Act 2012 provide the basis. CONFIRMED 2-1: entrants face the same registration and renewal procedures — automated advice does not escape the perimeter by being software. TTSEC's 2018 paper names six focus areas including 'review of algorithms and methodologies' — TTSEC expects to review your algorithms, so build explainable and auditable from day one: assumption provenance, versioned calculation logic, reproducible outputs. Design conclusion: the line is at securities-specific recommendations; budgeting, cash-flow, NIS/pension modelling, insurance needs analysis and goal tracking sit outside s.51. Posture (a) stay outside, architected so (b) register later is a switch. 3 claims from TTSEC's 2024 fintech-policy paper UNVERIFIED on a session limit — treat as leads: the register-under-an-existing-category position, the 'Automated Advice Tools' category explicitly covering aggregator-plus-advice platforms (which would describe this exact architecture), and the Innovation Hub + Regulatory Sandbox path.

nodes.label: eMoney 'Confidence Age' Monte Carlo metric
nodes.rationale: CONFIRMED 3-0 — the age at which a client's Monte Carlo probability-of-success dips below the advisor's chosen threshold. Reveals the engine shape: a whole-plan Monte Carlo score projected across the lifetime, surfaced as an age rather than '83% success'. Copy the pattern, not the name. Trial count, return methodology (historical bootstrap vs parametric) and per-goal probabilities remain unpublished and are not blocking — pick a defensible methodology and document it; being MORE transparent than eMoney is a differentiator.

nodes.rationale: TOTAL GAP, flagged as the highest-stakes question and item 10 returned NOTHING. No TTSEC guidance, no Central Bank guidance, no commentary on whether BIR-approved deferred annuities fall within the Securities Act 2012 definition of 'security'. This is a gap, not a negative finding — the volume of verified tax/NIS detail must not obscure it. Evidential position: founder (CBTT-registered agent, 13+ yrs) says annuities are part of the life licence; consistent with Tatil's disclaimer and Round 2's narrowing of 'investment advice' to securities; NO documentary corroboration and NO contradiction found.
nodes.norm_label: annuities: insurance act vs securities act — total gap

nodes.label: NIS reform 2026 — scope is exactly two things
nodes.rationale: CONFIRMED 3-0. Changed exactly two things: the contribution rate (13.2 -> 16.2 eff. 5 Jan 2026 -> 19.2 in 2027, split 1/3 employee / 2/3 employer) and retirement age (60 -> 65, +1yr every 2yrs from Jan 2028, reaching 65 in 2036). Did NOT touch the 750 threshold, increments, minimum pension, grant formula, or ceiling. The 9th review recommended the age change over 2025-2060; it was implemented FASTER (2028-2036). The 19.2%/2027 figure is PROVISIONAL (2-1).
nodes.norm_label: nis reform 2026 — scope is exactly two things

nodes.label: CARE conversion — the reform that would invalidate the engine
nodes.rationale: NIBTT's 8th Actuarial Review (published Sept 2012, valuation date 30 June 2010) recommended converting the earnings-class system to career-average revalued earnings (CARE) and, conditional on that, cutting the pension threshold from 750 to 260 weeks. NEITHER implemented. Useful twice over: it confirms the current 16-class / basic+increment / 750-week architecture is stable, and it names the single reform that would invalidate large parts of the engine if it ever lands.
nodes.norm_label: care conversion — the reform that would invalidate the engine

nodes.label: NIS qualifying conditions (150/50-in-3, 5-of-last-7, 750)
nodes.rationale: From the NIBTT training transcript: (1) 150 total contributions with 50 in the last 3 years, OR (2) employed 5 of the last 7 years, and (3) 750 contributions minimum for a pension. '7 years gates eligibility. Lifetime averaging sets the amount.' Two different rules, easily conflated — the engine must implement both, separately. Also confirmed: contributions remain mandatory past 750; NIBTT offers 23 benefits.

nodes.label: Age 60-64 cessation rule
nodes.rationale: CONFIRMED from source, and survives the discrediting of its parent document. Age 60-64: must cease insurable employment to claim. Age 65: paid whether you retire or not. Once claimed at 60-64, the pensioner 'will continue to receive such pension even if he returns to insurable employment before he attains age 65'. Payment starts from the Monday of the week retirement age was reached and continues monthly for life. Interacts with Class Z: a retiree drawing pension who returns to work attracts the reduced employer-paid Class Z rate.

nodes.label: Three working-note markdown files contradict each other
nodes.rationale: Parameter drift inside the project's own notes. Class XVI monthly pension per source: 'NIS Pension Calculation Research.md' (50%-of-earnings method) $6,799 — but its own text says the pension 'appears to be' ~50%, an inference, not a rule; the transcript describes a lookup table, not a formula. 'NIS Pension Amounts - Corrected.md' $5,500 — a salary->pension band table with no methodology and no source, titled 'Corrected', implying authority it doesn't document. 'NIS_Research_Findings.md' $10,000-12,000 — self-labelled 'estimated' and implausible against a Class XVI basic of ~$4,079. NONE should be encoded. The authoritative chain is: NIBTT published dated benefit schedule -> basic + increments per class -> lifetime-average class lookup. One useful corroboration: the first file independently agrees averaging is over ALL contributions, matching the transcript.
nodes.norm_label: three working-note markdown files contradict each other

nodes.label: s.6(l) cross-border hosting constraint
nodes.rationale: CONFIRMED 3-0 and LIVE TODAY. s.6 sets twelve General Privacy Principles binding all persons who handle, store or process personal information; principle (l) permits disclosure outside T&T only to jurisdictions with regulation and comparable safeguards. EU/UK (GDPR) reads as comfortably comparable; US-only hosting is a harder argument. CONFIRMED 3-0 for the future: unproclaimed s.69 would bind anyone collecting personal information IN T&T or FROM individuals in T&T or via a T&T intermediary — a scope capturing the app even if hosted abroad. Build to Part IV now; proclamation is a switch someone can flip.

nodes.source_location: GoldSpoon Gift — technical setup / plan family

Nothing is known of its mechanics, dates, COI table, or whether it is still sold. Source also references a 'Cashbuilder I' (CBI) as a further legacy generation. Do not encode any behaviour for this product; treat as a lead for document discovery only.

nodes.label: Convertible Level Term / Level Convertible Term to Age
nodes.rationale: EXTRACTED from the commission schedule catalog: Convertible Level Term 10/15/20/25 yr; Level Convertible Term to Age 60/65/70 aligning cover to retirement or mortgage horizon. 20-Year Convertible Term pays 35% first-year commission. Right for a temporary need with a known end date — income replacement while children are dependent, mortgage-matched cover, protection to retirement. Cheapest cover per dollar. The rate grid quantifies it: T65 for M/NS/35/$500k is $144.77/mo. T65 carries a $30.89/month policy fee ($360/yr), matching the WL and Endowment specs exactly.
nodes.norm_label: convertible level term / level convertible term to age

nodes.label: Limited-Pay Whole Life
nodes.rationale: EXTRACTED: pay 10/15/20/25/30 yr, or paid-up at 55/60/65. Retire the premium before you retire the income — right for someone who wants cover for life but no premiums in retirement. PERVERSE INCENTIVE recorded in the Whole Life 2023 spec: a shorter pay period HALVES first-year commission (30% at 10-14yr vs 60% at life/25-30yr), so the agent is paid LEAST for the limited-pay structure that often suits the client best. This is an independent firewall justification alongside destiny_commission_conflict. LP65 is one of the two products with a complete rate grid (64 quotes).

nodes.label: Group Life / Group Deferred Annuity
nodes.source_location: Group life / group pension / deposit administration
nodes.rationale: EXTRACTED. Employer-sponsored death cover — the 1-2x salary most employees have and lose on job change. THE PROTECTION-GAP ENGINE: group life reduces 50% at age 66 and TERMINATES AT 70, with no post-retirement cover. Most employed clients are underinsured AND about to lose what they have. Described as the single best prospecting insight for the individual-cover conversation, and it answers Tolani objection #33 ('My company has provided me insurance') with a verified fact rather than a rebuttal. The protection gap is the organizing concept: need - (in-force cover + group cover that will lapse at 70) = the gap the package fills.

nodes.label: Deposit Administration
nodes.rationale: EXTRACTED from the commission schedule: pooled employer retirement fund, tiered by fund size (<=30k / next 30k / >60k). Economics only — the commission schedule shows economics, not features. No product spec seen.

nodes.label: CI / Disability / Income Protection Riders
nodes.rationale: EXTRACTED, spec-sourced. Whole Life 2023 riders: Waiver of Premium (max issue 50, expires 60); Accidental Death (<=2x base, cap $500k, max issue 55, expires 65); AD&D (same limits, MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE with AD); Term coverage; Critical Illness (entry 17, max entry 50/55/60 for plans at 60/65/70); Refund of Premium on the CI rider. Cashbuilder II riders: AD, AD&D, TDWP, WPDDP, DIR (Disability Income Rider — $1,000/month per $100,000 SI, issue 20-55, expires 60, 6-month elimination period). STRUCTURAL CHOICE the engine must model: CI is available BOTH standalone (LifeSPAN) and as a rider on Whole Life — riders are typically cheaper attached than standalone. Commission is age-banded (35% at 0-50 down to 20% at 61+), reflecting real underwriting economics.

nodes.label: Publicsaver Life / Publicsaver DA
nodes.rationale: AMBIGUOUS — economics only, no product spec. Publicsaver Life is a hybrid split into a savings portion and an insurance portion, commissioned separately (savings 5%/yr, insurance 35% yr1). Publicsaver DA is a savings-oriented deferred annuity. Listed as an OPEN CONFIRMATION in the knowledge base: 'Publicsaver / Platinum Edge product mechanics from brochures (we have economics, not features).' Platinum Edge has since been resolved by its spec; Publicsaver has not.

nodes.label: Cashbuilder COI Rate Table (Annual Premium Rates per $1,000 Sum Assured)
nodes.rationale: MUST BE VERIFIED AGAINST THE SOURCE PDF BEFORE ENCODING — the OCR has DIGIT NOISE. Found in Appendix I of the GoldSpoon Gift spec, headed 'TATIL LIFE CASHBUILDER ASSURANCE — ANNUAL PREMIUM RATES PER $1,000 SUM ASSURED', ages 0-60, four columns (M-NS / M-S / F-NS / F-S). Full table at .firecrawl/ocr/GoldSpoon_Gift_-_Product_Specification_(Draft)_-_Jan_2008.txt. Known corrupted cells: age 33 M-NS reads 'al'; age 22 F-S reads '6.46' while age 21 reads '6.25' — plausible but unconfirmed. M-NS per $1,000: 5.56@25 -> 7.55@35 -> 10.55@45 -> 12.43@55 -> 20.06@60. COI QUADRUPLES between 25 and 60, and the curve steepens sharply after 55 (12.43 -> 20.06 in five years, +61%). Smoker rates are roughly DOUBLE non-smoker at every age (M-S 10.91@25, 24.71@55, 39.98@60). Female materially lower (F-NS 3.65@25, 8.11@55, 12.90@60). This closes the knowledge base's biggest gap ('COI rate tables — the specs describe the mechanic but don't publish the rates') and turns the rising-COI thesis from hypothesis into a rate table. The corpus rule stands: this is OCR, it is a LEAD, not a source of truth — the same rule has already caught three errors.

nodes.label: Policy X-ray — Legacy Cashbuilder as Highest-Value Target
nodes.rationale: INFERRED but strongly evidenced and stated independently in two files. The workflow: find every Cashbuilder on a client's book -> request an in-force illustration -> identify the ones projected to lapse. The knowledge base HYPOTHESISED this ('every legacy Cashbuilder the Policy X-ray finds may be heading for lapse right now, and nobody knows'); the CBIII spec CONFIRMS the ingredients (10.5% sale assumption, 4% floor, explicit positive-accumulation-or-lapse condition); the GoldSpoon COI table SUPPLIES the rising-cost curve that consumes the accumulation. Real service, real review trigger, and something no US tool will ever do for a Tatil Cashbuilder — the localization moat in concrete form.
nodes.norm_label: policy x-ray — legacy cashbuilder as highest-value target

nodes.label: Guaranteed Purchase Option
nodes.rationale: EXTRACTED from the authoritative GoldSpoon spec (OCR): 'Guaranteed Purchase Option included in all policies at no cost.' The child gets a guaranteed right to buy more cover later WITHOUT UNDERWRITING. Described in-source as a genuinely valuable, uncopyable planning lever: insure the child at age 1 and their future insurability is locked regardless of what health develops. Conceptually the same future-insurability mechanic as term convertibility, arrived at from the opposite end of the product range.

nodes.label: The Core Suitability Principle
nodes.source_location: The core suitability principle (encode this as a guardrail)
nodes.rationale: ENCODE AS A GUARDRAIL. Verbatim: 'Selling expensive permanent cover when cheaper term would meet the need — without disclosing the term option — is a recognized mis-selling pattern.' This is the exact conflict the commission firewall exists to prevent (whole life 60% vs term 35%). THE ENGINE'S RULE: when term satisfies the need, term must appear among the three options WITH ITS LOWER COST SHOWN, even when a permanent product also fits. Omitting the cheaper option that works is the failure mode — and 'no silent truncation' already forbids it. Packaging corollary: the right answer is usually a COMBINATION — term ladder against declining obligation (25/20/15-yr stacked to step down as the mortgage amortizes and children age out), whole life floor for the permanent piece, annuity for retirement timed inside 50-70, CI/disability rider on the base policy for the health-shock need.

nodes.label: Convertibility (future insurability lever)
nodes.rationale: MECHANIC IS UNIVERSAL, WINDOW IS NOT — a partially verified rule. 'The killer feature is convertibility: conversion to permanent needs no medical exam and preserves the original health rating from inception.' So a healthy 30-year-old can buy cheap term now and lock the right to permanent cover later EVEN IF THEIR HEALTH DETERIORATES — buy the option now, exercise it if life changes. WARNING: conversion windows are CARRIER-SPECIFIC (US Guardian defaults to 5 years + an Extended Conversion Rider); T&T carrier windows MUST BE CONFIRMED PER PRODUCT — the no-exam/preserved-rating mechanic is universal, the window is not. Listed as an open confirmation. Becomes a modelled product attribute in ProductCatalog: it is a genuine planning lever, and no US tool localizes it to these T&T products.

nodes.label: AM Best Affirmation of Tatil's Credit Ratings
nodes.rationale: EXTRACTED from tatil.co.tt: 'AM Best affirms credit ratings of Trinidad and Tobago Insurance Limited' — described as a real trust asset for the CLICO-scarred market. Its engine value is named in the OCR corpus: it answers Tolani objections #36 ('What if the insurance company goes bankrupt?') and #19 ('How do I know an insurance company will pay my claims?') with a SPECIFIC AND LOCAL fact, where Tolani's own answer is generic ('governments and institutions ensure no insurance company goes bust'). Specific-and-local is far stronger than generic in this market. This is the CLICO trust layer with a named trigger.
nodes.norm_label: am best affirmation of tatil's credit ratings

nodes.label: Tolani Objection Playbook (37 numbered objections)
nodes.author: Tolani
nodes.rationale: 163pp, 130,923 chars — the most directly useful material for the AIExplanationService. A complete objection taxonomy from a practitioner. ENCODING RULE: the Tolani/Maritime/Guardian material is PERSUASION LITERATURE — it belongs at the AI edges ONLY, NEVER in the decision path. The payoff is that four objections map onto findings already sourced and verified, so the engine can answer them with EVIDENCE RATHER THAN PERSUASION: #33 'My company has provided me insurance' -> group life reduces 50% at 66 and terminates at 70; #36/#19 bankruptcy and claims-paying -> AM Best affirms Tatil's ratings; #34 'I'd rather put money in a bank' -> Platinum Edge guarantees 2.5%, Destiny Option 1 guarantees 2%, and the TT$60,000 deduction applies to approved annuities but not a bank account; #8/#9/#10 'no money'/'too expensive' -> the leak ('$1,300 leaves every month and you can't name it'). Companion caution: the Tolani Closing Playbook OCR is NOISY (heavily designed book, render duplicates text blocks; body pages readable, title/graphic pages garbage) — usable for concepts, NOT for verbatim quotation.
