nodes.rationale: Tesseract OCR 5.4 (via winget) + PyMuPDF 1.27 + pytesseract. Pipeline at graphify-out/ocr.py — renders at 200 DPI, uses native text where present (free/perfect), OCRs only scanned pages. Output in .firecrawl/ocr/. Extracted ~470,000 characters across 10 previously-unreadable documents: Tolani Objection Playbook (163pp/130,923), Tolani Sales Maximizer (74pp/114,434), Tolani Closing Playbook (75pp/109,392, noisy), Maritime Sales Presentation (92pp/60,171), GoldSpoon Gift spec (8pp/7,678), Guardian Importance of Income (8pp/7,789), Saving for Retirement Self-Employed T&T (1pp/6,676), and brochures (Personal/Corporate Destiny, SPIA, Rest Assured, 4 img/7,885). THE GOVERNING RULE FOR EVERYTHING IT PRODUCES: 'This corpus is OCR — it is a LEAD, not a source of truth. Same rule that has now caught three errors.'

nodes.label: eMoney Premier
nodes.rationale: Vendor top-tier bundle = Plus (goals-based) + Pro (advanced cash-flow) + Premium Client Portal + mobile app. ~$5,000+/yr (Plus ~$2,600, Pro ~$4,100, per G2). Benchmarked as the functional target for an ORIGINAL competing T&T product — legal boundary explicitly stated: no code or pixel-exact design copying. Verification: multi-agent deep research, 5 search angles, 23 sources, 109 claims, top 25 adversarially verified by 3-vote panels, 24 confirmed / 1 refuted. Caveat recorded in source: feature claims rest on vendor marketing and onboarding docs — reliable for feature existence/packaging, silent on engine internals; short shelf life because eMoney ships actively.

nodes.label: Foundational Planning (eMoney)
nodes.rationale: Streamlined goals-based workflow producing plans 'with minimal client information and data input'. Middle of three planning UX tiers over ONE shared projection engine (Needs Analysis → Foundational → Advanced Planning/Decision Center). Design lesson: one engine, multiple UX depths; advisor switches methodology per client. eMoney is actively integrating Foundational and Decision Center (2025/2026 releases).

nodes.label: Advanced Planning (eMoney)
nodes.rationale: Models the current situation plus what-if scenarios (bear markets, spousal disability, retirement timing, inflation shocks). Medium confidence on framing per source. Deepest of the three UX tiers; entry point for the live-meeting flow (Advanced Planning → Goal Planner → Decision Center).

nodes.label: Goal Planner (eMoney)
nodes.rationale: Goal visualization layer; update slated early 2026. Verifier note recorded: Goal Planner and Decision Center are PRESENTATION/SCENARIO layers over one cash-flow engine, not independent engines — a replica must not build them as siloed engines.

nodes.label: Decision Center (eMoney)
nodes.rationale: Demonstrates recommendation impacts IN REAL TIME during live client meetings: interactive what-if toggling with immediate recalculation and multi-view dashboards — not batch report generation. Redesigned 2025 with Presentation View. Source's judgement: 'A replica's hardest build is this real-time scenario layer over the projection engine.' Directly inspires our PresentationMode / dual-view obligation counter.

nodes.label: eMoney Client Portal (two-tier)
nodes.rationale: Standard Client Portal included in every planning package; Premium Client Portal (launched April 2025) is a paid upgrade adding interactivity/engagement — bundled with Premier, add-on for lower tiers. No public price (sales-gated). Source verdict: 'a proven tiering pattern worth copying'. Includes a secure Vault (My Documents / Shared Documents, 30MB per-file limit, API-accessible). eMoney's historical differentiator is the portal/PFM experience, NOT the planning engine itself.

nodes.label: Account aggregation (held-away assets)
nodes.rationale: Treated by eMoney as foundational and operationally hard: it is the FIRST onboarding task on a new advisor's first coaching call, with a dedicated Week-1 'Optimizing Aggregation' one-on-one where the advisor selects a 'preferred primary data source'. eMoney reports a multi-year effort cutting aggregation service tickets by 70% — evidence of difficulty even at the market leader. 'Real-time' is marketing; practical replication spec is daily refresh with robust reconnection handling.

nodes.label: Attack surface #1 — aggregation reliability
nodes.rationale: HIGH CONFIDENCE, verified across three independent review sites (G2, Capterra, Software Advice, 2026). Most concrete recurring complaint: connections break or can't be established; clients repeatedly forced to re-authenticate; smaller institutions (credit unions) poorly covered. Reviewer language: 'very brittle', 'constant connection issues… to the point of making the software useless'. Trade-off recorded: it is simultaneously the clearest differentiation opportunity AND the hardest subsystem to build. Caveat in source: learning-curve and price complaints recur at least as often; this is merely the most concrete TECHNICAL complaint. Ultimately mooted for our product — the insurance-first wedge reads policy documents, not bank APIs.

nodes.label: Attack surface #2 — learning curve & silent modeling errors
nodes.rationale: HIGH CONFIDENCE. Kitces: 3–6 months to advisor proficiency on the cash-flow engine. Even 5-star fans call the interface 'kind of clunky' and note detailed modeling 'does take more time than less detailed planning tools'. Source's strategic read: 'This is exactly where RightCapital and MoneyGuidePro win — ease and speed-to-plan, not raw modeling power.' Action: build assumption-input guardrails/validation from day one. This is the bar the fact-find UX (§5) is explicitly set against.
nodes.norm_label: attack surface #2 — learning curve & silent modeling errors

nodes.label: Attack surface #3 — ready-made differentiation backlog
nodes.rationale: HIGH CONFIDENCE — named by 5-star reviewers ('even the fans'), which is what makes it credible: (1) no automatic debt-snowball rollover — paid-off debt payments must be manually reallocated; (2) imprecise mid-year transaction timing — a modeled home purchase starts the new mortgage January 1, over-projecting spending; (3) no healthcare-cost simulators (US complaint is IRMAA-specific; translates to a generic healthcare-cost-simulation requirement for the Caribbean); (4) no AI features (one reviewer's perception — eMoney could ship AI anytime, but it's an opening now); (5) G2 aggregate cons: 'lack of advanced features, making complex financial modeling challenging and imprecise' (6 mentions).

nodes.label: RightCapital
nodes.rationale: Competitor that beats eMoney on EASE and SPEED-TO-PLAN rather than raw modeling power. Named twice in the source as the proof that the learning-curve surface is real and commercially exploitable. Sets the UX bar for our fact-find.

nodes.label: MoneyGuidePro
nodes.rationale: eMoney's principal rival; eMoney is the #2 most-adopted planning software per Kitces surveys, competing with MoneyGuidePro. Also wins on ease/speed-to-plan rather than modeling depth.

nodes.label: T&T aggregation infeasibility — and its dissolution
nodes.rationale: The pivotal reframing: 'The aggregation blocker mostly dissolves too.' Round 2 confirmed no aggregator covers a single Caribbean bank — but an insurance-first product's data source is POLICY DOCUMENTS, not bank APIs. 'We never needed Plaid to read a policy schedule.' Consequences in §8: bank account aggregation explicitly not doing (confirmed infeasible); bank-statement import DEMOTED — getting statements from clients is a hard trust ask, whereas the POLICY ask survives because agents already collect exactly that data at the end of Meeting 1. Turning eMoney's hardest subsystem into a non-requirement is the core strategic move of the design.
nodes.norm_label: t&t aggregation infeasibility — and its dissolution

nodes.label: Tatil's Four Basic Needs
nodes.rationale: EXTRACTED from Tatil Life's real instrument: (1) retirement income, (2) financial security in event of death, (3) money to assist in event of critical illness, (4) money to assist with major expenses (education etc.). Design directive, verbatim: 'DO NOT INVENT A NEW FRAMEWORK.' This is the mental model T&T agents are already trained on and clients have already heard — adopting it makes the tool legible to an agent on day one, which is agent ramp (#10) for free. Independently corroborated by Principal's need-first concept indexing (a US carrier arriving at the same IA). Doubles as the spec's scope table: needs 1 and 2 are v1 IN, needs 3 and 4 are Next, and triage routes between them so the architecture doesn't change when 3 and 4 arrive.

nodes.label: T&T standardized needs formula
nodes.rationale: THE NeedsEngine spec, taken from a real T&T insurer rather than invented. TOTAL NEEDS = funeral + medical + outstanding loans + mortgage liquidation + rental income for 120 months + education expense + income continuation until last child attains 21. TOTAL ASSETS = savings + existing life insurance + other investments. INSURANCE NEED = NEEDS − ASSETS. Nets NIB survivors' benefits. Correctly OMITS the US estate-tax liquidity driver — T&T has no estate, inheritance or gift tax. Two conventions ('120 months' rental income, 'until last child attains 21') are LOCAL NORMS, NOT UNIVERSAL TRUTHS and belong in ParameterTables as named, dated, sourced values — never in code.

nodes.label: Triage checklist (Guardian's 16-item concern list)
nodes.rationale: Guardian opens with a 16-item concern checklist, self/spouse columns: 'Please tick which is of utmost concern to you currently to guide our discussion today.' Items: income protection, family income protection, life insurance, critical illness, funeral expense, mortgage planning (repay at term / on death / on critical illness), paying off debt, retirement, savings, children's education, health, car, property, contents. THE KEY MECHANISM: 'This is the mechanism that makes five questions, not twelve honest. You don't shorten the fact-find by asking less — you triage first and ask only what's relevant to what they pointed at.' Reduced to ~8 tiles in the spec. Note the checklist already asks about car, home, contents and health — if a client ticks one and we have nothing, that's a dead end we built ourselves (an argument for capturing general insurance).

nodes.label: The five questions
nodes.rationale: Screen 0 is triage, then five questions one at a time with the canvas reflecting: (1) Who depends on you? — 'A parent, a nephew, someone overseas. It doesn't have to be official.'; (2) What comes in, what goes out? — monthly income AND expense (Tatil captures both; most US tools only capture income); (3) What do you owe? — mortgage, loans, cards: balance, installment, years to go (Maritime's shape); (4) What do you already have? — THIS IS THE X-RAY, seeded from documents where available; (5) What would you want to happen? — one soft question, chosen by triage. Then budget via Guardian's % band anchor, verbatim. The soft questions are field-tested, not invented: 'What do you believe life insurance should do for you and your family?', 'If you suffered a long term disability for say 6 to 12 months, how would your bills be paid?', 'What are some of the things you plan to do when you retire? Paint a picture for me.' Requirements, not polish: never more than one question on screen; everything skippable; permission language; visible accomplishment.

nodes.label: Informal dependent (household obligation)
nodes.rationale: VALIDATION, not invention. Guardian already asks: 'If there was an immediate need to fund a major surgery for your parents or family members due to an accident or sickness, how would you help fund it?' The household obligation (#14) is ALREADY IN THE INCUMBENT'S SCRIPT — 'We're not inventing a need — we're making an existing, awkwardly-worded question visual and structured. That's a much safer bet than a novel insight.' Covers elderly parents, outside children, supported relatives overseas. The permission line 'It doesn't have to be official' is what lets someone name an outside child or a supported nephew — the household model earning its place in the UI.

nodes.label: Two-meeting sale (Discovery + Decision)
nodes.rationale: Guardian documents the process precisely. Discovery (~40 min): introduction, client introduces themselves, importance of income, fact-finding questionnaire (15 min), identify needs/wants/budget (15 min), summary, LIST OF WHAT TO BRING TO 2ND MEETING, schedule. Decision: changes since last meeting, review concerns, three alternative solutions (15 min), select solution (10 min), paperwork + first premium, medical exam, next steps. TWO CONSEQUENCES: (a) the client portal's job is THE GAP BETWEEN THE MEETINGS — structural role, not a nice-to-have; (b) 'List of what to bring for our 2nd meeting' is where the Policy X-ray lives — our wedge slots into an existing ritual rather than creating a new one. AMBIGUITY RESOLVED IN SPEC: PALIG's contact sheet tracks THREE appointment dates where Guardian documents two; practitioner confirmation says 'usually two, often three or more'. Therefore §3.3: DO NOT HARDCODE A STEP COUNT — 'the plan has a state, not a step number. The portal is the continuous line; meetings are punctuation.' A wizard that ends at step 2 either blocks the real conversation or forces the agent to lie to it. A six-meeting relationship is a supported path, not an error.

nodes.label: Three options, not one
nodes.rationale: Guardian's Decision Meeting agenda: 'Presentation of up to three (3) alternative solutions (15 mins)' then 'Selecting the solution that has the best benefits for your needs, wants and preferences (10 mins)'. Spec correction: RecommendationEngine → Package becomes → [Package × 3] with DIFFERENTIATED rationale. 'The sale is a CHOICE AMONG THREE, not an accept/reject of one.' Options must be meaningfully differentiated (e.g. maximum cover / balanced / lowest premium), not three cosmetic variants. Corroborated by Tolani's objection corpus: a choice among three generates fewer objections than accept/reject of one — 'the sale happens after the first no.'

nodes.label: Budget as percentage-of-income band
nodes.rationale: ⚠️ SPEC CORRECTION recorded in source: 'Our spec was wrong about Budget.' Guardian elicits budget as a % band with SOCIAL-PROOF ANCHORING, never as a dollar figure: 'Most of my clients spend between 10–15% of their income towards solving their needs. There are a fortunate few who can invest 16–25%... And some are on a tight budget and can only afford between 5–9%. Into which category would you fall?' The framing is deliberately engineered: 10–15% is 'most of my clients' (the norm and the default), 16–25% is 'a fortunate few' (aspirational, flatters), 5–9% is 'a tight budget' (the floor). Capture as % band, normalize to monthly TTD internally. Capturing a raw TTD figure THROWS THE ANCHORING MECHANIC AWAY. All product rates normalize to monthly before optimization regardless of the carrier's native billing frequency.

nodes.label: Suitability + affordability attestation
nodes.rationale: Tatil's existing client signature block, to be modeled on rather than invented: 'I certify that to the best of my knowledge the information provided above is correct. Based on the above review, I understand why the foregoing product(s) have been suggested as suitable for me and that I can afford to pay the ongoing premiums.' Both client and agent sign, both dated. THE CONSEQUENCE: it bundles SUITABILITY + AFFORDABILITY in one attestation — which is why affordability (#5) cannot be deferred as far as spec §8 originally planned. The signed record already asserts it, so v1 must at minimum capture monthly income and expense (fact-find Q2) and assert premium sustainability against them.

nodes.label: Tied-agent model (CBTT-registered, single carrier)
nodes.rationale: CONFIRMED IN WRITING by Tatil's own disclaimer: 'Tatil Life Assurance Limited... is a licensed financial institution regulated by the Central Bank of Trinidad & Tobago (CBTT). All of our Agents and Sales Representatives are registered with the CBTT and are only authorised to sell Tatil Life products.' Confirms all three at once: Central Bank regulation (NOT TTSEC), mandatory agent registration, and single-carrier tied distribution. 'Our segment decision holds.' Spec §2: tied agents first, brokers later — largest population; comparison features stay behind a flag so we don't offend the first buyer.

nodes.label: PALIG Personal Net Worth Calculator
nodes.rationale: Built 2012, last saved 2013. Verdict: LOAD-BEARING — 'contributes a scoring model and confirms a market convention.' Its value is that it independently validates mechanics we thought were novel: the benchmark allocation (identical to Maritime's, thirteen years apart), the usable-income leak, per-debt years-to-payoff, and a competing top-down needs methodology. Also supplies real T&T taxonomy labels and a disclaimer worth adopting: 'The calculated results are intended for illustrative purposes only; accuracy is not guaranteed. Please consult a financial professional for advice.' Caveat: its net-worth quality bands (Excellent 1M / Good 750k / Fair 500k / Poor 250k / Unacceptable 100k) are 2012 figures needing inflation adjustment before reuse.

nodes.label: T&T benchmark allocation (market-standard)
nodes.source_location: PALIG §1; factfinder-analysis Smaller findings; spec ParameterTables
nodes.rationale: Tax 15% · Loans 25% · Pension/Retirement 10% · Insurance-Life 5% · Insurance-General 5% · Savings+Investment 10% · Living Expense 30%. IDENTICAL across PALIG (2012) and Maritime (current) — two independent T&T insurers, fourteen years apart. 'This answers the question I raised about needing a Sagicor fact finder to distinguish convention from house style — IT'S CONVENTION. Encode it as a T&T benchmark with confidence.' Verified ✅ market-standard in the spec's ParameterTables table. Note the 5% General Insurance line is itself an argument that general insurance belongs in the picture — it's in the market-standard model already.

nodes.label: PALIG Quality Rater
nodes.rationale: Scores each budget category's variance from benchmark: Excellent (better than −5%) · Good (−15% to −6%) · Fair (−30% to −16%) · Poor (−45% to −31%) · Unacceptable (worse than −46%). Worked example: Loans at 34.2% vs 25% benchmark → variance −9.2% → 'Poor'; Living Expense at 13.2% vs 30% → 'Excellent'. ORIGINAL ARGUMENT FOR: it converts the exhaustive budget from data entry into A DIAGNOSIS THE CLIENT RECEIVES — 'it gives them something back for the work, which is exactly what makes optional homework get done.' SPEC OVERRULED IT: 'The Quality Rater is REPURPOSED, NOT SHIPPED AS DESIGNED. PALIG's Excellent→Unacceptable labels grade a client against a benchmark they never agreed to; a gentler word doesn't fix that. DROP the labels and the scorecard; KEEP the variance; express it in dollars; surface only the largest.' Resulting output: 'Loans take 34% of what you earn. Typical in T&T is 25%. That gap is $1,100 a month' — a fact, not a verdict, and it EXPLAINS THE LEAK rather than existing as a separate report card. 'No judgment to hide, so nothing needs hiding.'

nodes.label: Usable Income / the leak
nodes.rationale: PALIG computed it in 2012: Liability/Gross Income = 0.537 · Liability/Take home = 0.591 · Usable Income % = 0.409 · Usable Income $ = 2,925. 'That is our leak, computed thirteen years ago by a T&T insurer. THE MECHANIC IS VALIDATED, NOT NOVEL — which is reassuring rather than disappointing. Ours improves on it by DERIVING THE NUMBER CONVERSATIONALLY instead of demanding a filled form.' Instance of Feldman's 'make the abstract concrete' principle — turning an abstract obligation into a vivid specific number. Triage routes 'debt' to the leak as that journey's single headline insight. Also the answer to Tolani objections #8/9/10 (the no-money objections).

nodes.label: Per-debt years-to-payoff (ladder decline schedule)
nodes.rationale: PALIG tracks each debt with balance, end date, and computed years-to-payoff (e.g. Credit Union 1,500 → 2014-11-04 → 1.47 yrs; Mortgage 350,000 → 2016-01-21 → 2.68; Tertiary Education 50,000 → 2015-04-12 → 1.90). GAP THIS CLOSES: 'This is the input the laddering engine (#11) needs. Obligation declines on a known schedule as debts retire; the term ladder should step down to match. OUR SPEC ASSERTED LADDERING AGAINST DECLINING OBLIGATION WITHOUT SAYING WHERE THE DECLINE SCHEDULE COMES FROM. It comes from here.' Now consumed by NeedsEngine per spec §3.2.

nodes.label: T-T-Financial-Insurance-Hub repo
nodes.author: Kelsean868 (the founder)
nodes.rationale: Verdict: 'a substantial chunk of ParameterTables already written.' Five calculators, 100% HTML on GitHub Pages, SEO'd, public. 'The HTML is a prototype; THE LOGIC IS THE ASSET.' Supplies: PAYE brackets (personal allowance 90,000; 25% ≤1M, 30% >1M), the TT$60,000 combined NIS/annuity deduction cap (independently CONFIRMING Round 1's panel that killed the government site's stale TT$30,000 figure 0–3 — two independent sources now agree), 70% NIS deductibility (NEW — no such rule in our spec), Health Surcharge bands (4.80/wk ≤469.99/mo, 8.25/wk above — a deduction absent from our spec entirely), the REAL NIS pension formula (16 earnings classes with basicMonthly + incrementMonthly; increments = floor(excess/25); pension = basic + increments × increment; grant = totalMonetaryValue × 3), Section 134(6) corporate annuity logic, and PUBLIC SERVANTS' PENSION + GRATUITY (a separate regime covering a large share of T&T employment — another gap in our spec). Also a top-of-funnel asset: five public SEO'd calculators already live and indexed — someone computing their take-home pay or NIS pension is self-identifying as exactly the person who needs a needs analysis.

nodes.label: Dated parameter-tables discipline
nodes.source_location: The repo already implements our hardest rule; spec §3.2 ParameterTables
nodes.rationale: THE STRONGEST SELF-PROVING ARGUMENT IN THE PROJECT. The repo embeds 13 dated contribution-rate tables spanning 1972→2016 — that IS the 'no bare constants, always year-indexed and dated' discipline the spec demands, already built in production by the same author. AND YET the most recent table is 2016-09-05 while the true rate is 16.2% eff. 2026-01-05 rising to 19.2% in 2027, with retirement age phasing from 2028. 'The architecture is right; THE DATA HAS DRIFTED. This is the strongest possible argument for the spec's parameter discipline — the tables went stale in exactly the way we predicted, IN CODE WRITTEN BY SOMEONE WHO KNEW TO DATE THEM.' The spec escalates to three independent proofs: (1) the Ministry of Finance publishes a stale TT$30,000 cap that conflicts with current law; (2) the repo's own dated tables drifted anyway; (3) NIBTT's own site is internally inconsistent — its FAQ states the 2016 rate of 13.2% with no mention of 16.2%, while the TT$13,600 ceiling on that same page IS current: one page, one right constant and one wrong one, silently. THEREFORE: provenance is PER-PARAMETER, NOT PER-PAGE — every parameter carries its own source URL, retrieval date and review date; 'trusting a page is not a strategy'; a staleness check runs in CI. Rated High severity risk (parameter drift) in §7.

nodes.label: Real T&T taxonomy (verbatim labels)
nodes.rationale: Use verbatim — 'These are the labels a Trini recognizes.' EXPENSES: Food/Clothing · Education · Entertainment/Travelling · TSTT/WASA/T&TEC/CCTT · Life Insurance Premiums · General Insurance Premiums · Property Maintenance Fee · Reg. Pension/Annuity · Alimony/Maintenance · NIS. DEBTS: Credit Union Loans · Bank Loan · Mortgage/Rent · Tertiary Education Loans · Vehicle Loan · First Time Home Owners · Hire Purchase · Credit Card Debt/Overdraft. ASSETS: Bank Accounts · Fixed Deposits · Private Stock Shares · Bonds · Credit Union Shares · Life Insurance (CSV) · Money Market Funds · Income & Growth Funds (UTC) · Retirement Savings (CSV) · Real Estate · Real Estate–Time Share · Vehicle · Furniture & Appliances · Machinery & Equipment. INCOME: Monthly Salary/Pension · Mth tax-free special duty allowance · Other Income. 'Hire Purchase, First Time Home Owners, Credit Union Shares, tax-free special duty allowance, and the TSTT/WASA/T&TEC/CCTT grouping have NO US ANALOGUE.' Complements the contrast finding: the US textbook fact finder is the control group — it asks about IRAs, Social Security, revocable living trusts, durable powers of attorney and taxable-equivalent conversion, none of which exist in T&T. It's a precise inventory of what localization must strip out, and what every US tool would drag in.

nodes.label: Founder de-risks the spec's #1 risk
nodes.rationale: The repo's README identifies the author as A LICENSED INSURANCE AGENT WITH 13+ YEARS of retirement planning experience. The spec named rate-catalog data as the single HIGH risk — 'outside our control', to be solved by finding a design partner who is also a data supplier. THAT PARTNER IS THE FOUNDER: design partner in-house · first user in-house · rate book — an agent has one · recommender of record — already registered with the CBTT · 13 years T&T domain expertise · distribution — five public SEO'd calculators already live. Spec §7 accordingly DOWNGRADES the rate-data risk High → Medium, while keeping the discipline: RateProvider interface, seed with ONE carrier and 2–3 products; adding carriers = data entry, not engineering; 'DO NOT ATTEMPT TO LAUNCH WITH THE WHOLE MARKET.' The founder's practitioner knowledge also settled the annuity licence question that research got wrong — establishing the rule that when verification contradicts a practitioner, go to source before overriding them.

nodes.label: 37-objection taxonomy
nodes.source_location: derived from OCR of the Tolani Objection Playbook (post-dates this document)
nodes.rationale: INFERRED/AMBIGUOUS PROVENANCE — the 37-objection taxonomy is the OCR yield of the Tolani Objection Playbook and is NOT itself described in sales-craft-library.md, which still lists the playbooks as un-OCR'd. Recorded per instruction; verify against the OCR output before relying on the numbering. 37 numbered objections, FOUR OF WHICH MAP ONTO VERIFIED FACTS — which is what makes them answerable by the ENGINE'S evidence rather than by persuasion: #33 'group life covers me' → group life reduces 50% at 66 and TERMINATES AT 70, so gap = need − (in-force individual cover + group cover zeroed from 70); #36 post-CLICO bankruptcy fear → answerable via AM Best rating; #34 'the bank pays more' → Platinum Edge's 2.5% guarantee; #8/#9/#10 the no-money objections → answered by the leak (the usable-income mechanic showing where the money already goes). CRITICAL BOUNDARY: these four are answerable BECAUSE a verified fact answers them — the taxonomy supplies the REGISTER for the reply, never the substance. An objection answered with persuasion instead of evidence is the failure mode the persuasion firewall exists to prevent.

nodes.label: Household (root aggregate)
nodes.rationale: Root aggregate. Models the people who depend on the client, their relationships, obligations, income and ages. Supports MULTI-GENERATIONAL AND INFORMAL DEPENDENTS (elderly parents, outside children, supported relatives overseas) — NOT A NUCLEAR COUPLE. This is the deliberate departure from US tooling and it is validated by Guardian's existing parents-surgery question. Pure — no I/O, no network, fully unit-testable. Interface: Household value object, built incrementally by the fact-find. Depends on nothing. In MVP (#14).

nodes.label: PolicyLedger
nodes.rationale: Holds the client's in-force AND LAPSED policies — insurer, product, cover, premium, riders, cash value, beneficiary, status. Interface: .add(Policy), .inForceCover(), .byInsurer(). Depends on nothing — 'Populated by manual entry or AI ingestion — IT DOESN'T CARE WHICH.' That indifference is the architectural guarantee that AIIngestionService remains an accelerant rather than a dependency.

nodes.label: NeedsEngine
nodes.rationale: Household → NeedsProfile. Pure function computeNeeds(household, params). T&T-localized; THE FORMULA IS NOT INVENTED — it is the standardized T&T instrument from Tatil Life. Depends on ParameterTables INJECTED, NEVER IMPORTED. Load-bearing design decisions: (a) ✅ MUST MODEL NIS ⊕ SCP JOINTLY — confirmed from primary source, gate lifted; the engine must refuse to land a client just over a cliff (2,500/3,500/4,500/5,500) without flagging it — a CORRECTNESS FIX, NOT AN ENHANCEMENT; (b) SUPPORTS BOTH T&T METHODOLOGIES SHOWN SIDE BY SIDE — Tatil's bottom-up needs formula (headline) and PALIG's top-down coverage − net worth (cross-check). 'They will disagree. TWO CREDIBLE NUMBERS WITH A STATED BASIS BEATS ONE NUMBER WITH A HIDDEN METHOD — and it directly attacks eMoney's silent-assumption weakness.' Caveat: insuring to net worth is closer to estate replacement than income replacement and is arguably the weaker method — present as cross-check, not headline; (c) consumes per-debt years-to-payoff as the ladder's decline schedule. Testing: golden-file tests against hand-computed T&T cases; assert no estate-tax driver.

nodes.label: GapCalculator
nodes.rationale: NeedsProfile − PolicyLedger.inForceCover() → Gap. 'TRIVIAL CODE; IT IS THE MONEY SHOT OF THE WHOLE PRODUCT.' The clearest statement in the spec that value lives in the inputs' correctness, not the arithmetic. Depends on NeedsEngine and PolicyLedger.

nodes.label: ProductCatalog
nodes.rationale: Structured store of T&T life products — insurer, product type, rate tables (age/sex/smoker/band), riders, underwriting rules, non-medical limits, exclusions, and a STATUS FIELD (new/legacy, so the X-ray can identify old products like Cashbuilder on a client's book). Real T&T taxonomy — Term: convertible level (10/15/20/25 yr), term-to-age (60/65/70) — CONVERTIBILITY IS A MODELLED ATTRIBUTE, 'a real planning lever no US tool localizes'. Permanent: whole life, limited-pay whole life. Accumulation: endowment (15–30 yr), fund-linked deferred annuity, savings+insurance hybrids (Publicsaver). Specialist: final expense / simplified issue (Rest Assured, LifeSpan Lite), riders (CI/disability/income protection). Group: group life, group annuity, deposit administration. Interface: RateProvider — quote(product, applicant, coverAmount) → Premium | NoRates. The NoRates return is what makes 'no silent truncation' expressible in the type. Depends on external rate data (§7).

nodes.label: RecommendationEngine
nodes.rationale: (Gap, Budget, Catalog, Constraints) → [Package × 3] + Rationale. Constrained optimization over a POLICY LADDER: term laddering against declining obligation, a whole-life floor for permanent need, CI riders. Maximize coverage adequacy subject to totalMonthlyPremium ≤ budget. DETERMINISTIC AND REPRODUCIBLE — 'same inputs produce byte-identical output, always. THAT PROPERTY IS AUDITABILITY.' Load-bearing rules from the verified product knowledge base: THE ANTI-MIS-SELLING GUARDRAIL — when term satisfies the need, term MUST appear among the three options with its lower cost shown, EVEN WHEN a permanent product also fits; recommending permanent without surfacing the cheaper term that works is a recognized mis-selling pattern. 'THIS IS THE CLIENT-SIDE TWIN OF THE COMMISSION FIREWALL.' Annuity maturity: age 50 is a STATUTORY FLOOR (refuse to model maturity <50); age 70 is the exemption edge (WARN on maturity >70 — legal, but forfeits the 2026 exemption) — 'these are DIFFERENT RULES, NOT ONE WINDOW.' Convertibility is a lever; carrier conversion windows must come from ProductCatalog, never assumed. Simplified-issue graded benefit: never present final-expense/no-medical as first-day full cover. Universal life is THE ONE PRODUCT THAT CAN SILENTLY COLLAPSE. The protection gap includes group cover that will lapse. Property tests: never exceeds budget; never recommends an ineligible product; always produces a rationale; NEVER SILENTLY DROPS A PRODUCT.

nodes.label: SuitabilityRecord
nodes.rationale: The Market Conduct artifact — inputs, rules fired, alternatives considered, rejection reasons, rates-as-of date, catalog version. KEY DESIGN: 'EMITTED BY RecommendationEngine, NOT BUILT SEPARATELY. COMPLIANCE FALLS OUT OF THE RECOMMENDATION FOR FREE.' This is only possible because the engine is deterministic — a compliance artifact generated by a nondeterministic process would prove nothing. Modeled on Tatil's existing attestation, which both client and agent sign and date and which bundles suitability + affordability. Because commission is held but never optimized on, the record can AFFIRMATIVELY STATE the recommendation was made without reference to commission — a Market Conduct gold standard and a complete answer to 'why this product?'. In MVP (#3, free).

nodes.label: ParameterTables
nodes.rationale: Year-indexed, dated, sourced T&T constants; seeded from the T-T-Financial-Insurance-Hub repo. HARD RULE: 'no T&T parameter is ever a constant in code — and PROVENANCE IS PER-PARAMETER, NOT PER-PAGE.' Every parameter carries its own source URL, retrieval date and review date; a staleness check runs in CI; tests assert every parameter has a date and a source and that no bare numeric constants appear in domain code. VERIFICATION STATUSES CARRIED: ✅3–0 verified — Health Surcharge + exemptions (under 16 · 60 and over · pension-only income; 'material: never charge a 62-year-old'), TT$60,000 cap, NIS 16.2% eff. 2026-01-05, 16 classes & 13,600 ceiling, pension formula structure, whole-working-life averaging (NIBTT training transcript, verbatim), 750-contribution threshold, minimum pension 3,000/mo eff. 2012-02-01, Retirement Grant, retirement age 60→65 reaching 65 in 2036, benchmark allocation, SCP bands/age/residency (scraped from social.gov.tt), NIS pension = SCP assessed income (grant excluded). 🔴 BLOCKING — PENSION_RATES outdated: the repo holds the stale 2008 benefit table (335.83…2,475.70) while the current 2016 table (eff. 2016-09-05, Class I 566.72 … XVI 4,079.40) sits under /Contribution_Rates/; current values ~69% higher; 'UNDERSTATED NIS → OVERSTATED GAP → RECOMMENDS MORE PRODUCT — a real mis-selling exposure on a signed suitability record.' 🔴 NIS 2016 increments UNRESOLVED — do not guess. 🟡 PROVISIONAL — 19.2% from Jan 2027 (budget announcement + arithmetic, NO GAZETTED SCHEDULE; never show 2027 figures as settled); Finance Bill 2026 annuity exemption (BILL, not Act — passed House 28–0 with 13 abstentions June 2026; Senate + assent unverified; code conditional on assent). ⚪ UNVERIFIED — personal allowance 90,000, PAYE bands, 70% NIS deductibility. ⚠️ 'Do not encode the NIS Stuff markdown files' — three of them give three different answers for the same figure. Authoritative chain: published dated NIBTT benefit schedule → basic + increments → lifetime-average class lookup. KEY STRUCTURAL FINDING: NIBTT runs TWO rate systems with different rules — CONTRIBUTION rates are ERA-SELECTED (dated sets 1972–2006, 2008–2012, 2013–2014, 2016 @13.2%, 2026 @16.2%; the 2016 page is live because contributions Sept 2016→Jan 2026 were made at 13.2% — current for its period, not stale), while BENEFIT rates are A SINGLE CURRENT TABLE APPLIED AT QUALIFICATION ('Rates … for persons qualifying on or after 7th January 2008'). Both halves of the repo are architecturally correct; only defect is missing provenance. METHODOLOGICAL SCARS RECORDED IN THE SPEC ITSELF: a prior round refuted the SCP bands 1–2 and declared the interaction unverifiable, downgrading a CORRECT insight to 'fiction'; another claimed 3–0 that the benefit rates were '18 years obsolete' and FABRICATED replacement figures — 'had it been actioned it would have written a real mis-selling bug into the engine.' RULES: 'when an agency publishes the number, SCRAPE THE AGENCY — a vote over search results is not evidence'; 'SCRAPING IS NOT VERIFICATION EITHER — ONE PAGE IS A SAMPLE. When a number is disputed, find EVERY page the issuer publishes it on and reconcile. Agencies contradict themselves; NIBTT demonstrably does'; 'a unanimous vote is not truth'; 'when verification contradicts a practitioner, GO TO SOURCE BEFORE OVERRIDING THEM.' Consequence: 'Every single-page confirmed-from-source claim in this project — INCLUDING THE SCP BANDS — needs a second source.'

nodes.label: CommissionCalculator
nodes.rationale: Agent-facing, STRICTLY DOWNSTREAM. Given a recommendation ALREADY FIXED, computes the agent's expected commission from the carrier schedule (heaped first-year + renewal trail; e.g. Tatil Whole Life 60/15/10/5/5/2.5, Destiny annuity 5/3/1+trail). 'Depends on a FIXED recommendation + the carrier commission schedule. NEVER SITS UPSTREAM OF RecommendationEngine.'

nodes.label: AIIngestionService
nodes.rationale: Document → structured Policy. 'AN ACCELERANT, NEVER A DEPENDENCY.' Structured manual entry is the PRIMARY path (~90 seconds per policy). Output is ALWAYS agent-confirmed before entering the ledger; tests assert unconfirmed extractions never reach the ledger. §7 risk: OCR of heterogeneous policy documents is hard (Medium) — 'manual entry is the primary path; OCR is an accelerant added AFTER SEEING REAL DOCUMENTS. MVP DOES NOT BET ON IT.'

nodes.label: ClientPortal
nodes.rationale: Read view: household, policies, need, gap, proposed package. ITS STRUCTURAL JOB IS THE GAP BETWEEN THE MEETINGS — 'Not a nice-to-have — that's its structural purpose, and it's why the agent-led marketplace model is right.' 'The portal is the continuous line; meetings are punctuation.' Also the true second screen for the client via their phone — but 'the MVP MUST NOT DEPEND on that being present in the room.' In MVP; included in the first milestone deliberately.

nodes.label: PresentationMode (obligation counter dual view)
nodes.rationale: A client-safe render of the agent's live session — same data, different view, explicit toggle. Mirrors eMoney's Decision Center Presentation View (2025 redesign). DECISION: agent sees the obligation counter live; client sees it on reveal. TWO REQUIRED MECHANICS make this legitimate rather than sneaky: (1) presentation mode is A HARD TOGGLE, NOT A HOPE — same session, client-safe render, entered deliberately; (2) THE AGENT'S NUMBER STAYS QUIET — a small glanceable figure in a status bar, not a banner. THE T&T-SPECIFIC REASONING: 'In T&T, agent and client are frequently at one kitchen table looking at ONE LAPTOP. If the client catches the number, they must see A PRACTITIONER'S INSTRUMENT PANEL, NOT A CONCEALED SALES GAUGE. In a market still carrying the CLICO wound, getting this wrong doesn't cost a sale — IT COSTS TRUST.' Also resolves the §7 risk 'client under-reports dependents to game the counter' — the client doesn't see the number while building.

nodes.label: Policy X-ray (the wedge)
nodes.rationale: THE CHOSEN WEDGE. Rationale as stated: 'the ONLY wedge that pays both sides on day one; builds the data asset everything else needs; UNCOPYABLE BY INCUMBENTS.' Fact-find Q4 ('What do you already have?') IS the X-ray. Its structural genius is that it slots into an EXISTING RITUAL: agents already end Meeting 1 with 'here's what to bring next time' — 'our wedge doesn't create a new behaviour, IT INSTRUMENTS ONE THAT EXISTS.' This is also why the policy ask survives while bank-statement import was demoted: getting statements from clients is a hard trust ask; agents already collect exactly the policy data. Extension recommended: capture GENERAL policies immediately too — now cheaper because the data shapes exist in General_Raters_Portal; premiums feed the leak and the 5% benchmark, renewal dates are review triggers.

nodes.label: Deterministic core
nodes.rationale: The organizing principle: AI ingestion → [DETERMINISTIC CORE — decides everything] → AI explanation. TEST OF CORRECTNESS: 'IF BOTH AI SERVICES FAIL, THE PRODUCT STILL WORKS AND STILL RECOMMENDS CORRECTLY — it is merely less convenient. IF THAT CEASES TO BE TRUE, THE ARCHITECTURE HAS BEEN VIOLATED.' WHY NON-NEGOTIABLE: TTSEC's 2018 robo-advice paper lists 'review of algorithms and methodologies' as a regulatory focus area; the Central Bank's Market Conduct Guideline (July 2023) imposes parallel suitability duties. 'THE MODEL DECIDED IS NOT AN AUDITABLE METHODOLOGY. AN LLM THAT HALLUCINATES A COVER AMOUNT IS NOT A BUG — IT IS A MIS-SELLING EVENT.' Enforced by test: identical inputs run twice, diff the output, must be byte-identical.

nodes.label: AI at the edges
nodes.rationale: Locked decision: 'AI at the edges, NEVER IN THE DECISION PATH' — rationale given as regulatory auditability (§4). AI is admitted at exactly two boundaries: ingestion (document → Policy, always agent-confirmed) and explanation (engine output → plain language, never decides). The same shape as the commission firewall and the persuasion firewall: admit the capability, bar it from the decision. Note the differentiation-backlog finding that eMoney has 'no AI features' — the opening exists, but this posture deliberately declines to exploit it in the decision path.

nodes.label: Agent is recommender of record
nodes.rationale: 'The registered agent, ALWAYS. Keeps the vendor outside intermediary registration.' 'SOFTWARE PROPOSES; THE AGENT DISPOSES.' The agent's review/adjust/approve step in Meeting 2 is THE REGULATORY HINGE — 'Not optional, not skippable.' Note 'insurance consultants' are themselves a registered category under the Insurance Act — the vendor must not act as one. Companion rule — NO SILENT TRUNCATION: if the optimizer couldn't evaluate a product (missing rates) it must say 'cannot evaluate product X — no rates'; 'silently omitting reads as we considered everything when we didn't — THE EXACT MIS-SELLING FAILURE MODE.' Every recommendation carries provenance: rates as of date, source, catalog version, rules fired, alternatives rejected and why. Legal review required before launch on the investment-linked boundary, whether the software constitutes intermediary activity, and Data Protection Act s.6(l) hosting (only Part I is proclaimed, but s.6(l) is live: personal information disclosed outside T&T may only go to jurisdictions with comparable safeguards — EU/UK reads comfortably comparable, US-only is a harder argument; build to the unproclaimed Part IV anyway since s.69 would capture this product even if hosted abroad, and 'proclamation is a switch someone can flip'). CBTT payment-services perimeter does not enumerate read-only data aggregation — a product that never moves money is likely outside PSP registration, but that is an argument from omission on the regulator's own page; confirm with counsel.

nodes.label: Conversation drives, canvas reflects
nodes.rationale: The locked fact-find UX decision. 'The most-hated moment in insurance sales. eMoney's answer is a dense form that takes 3–6 months to master and that its own 5-star reviewers call kind of clunky. RightCapital beats it on ease, not power. THAT IS THE BAR.' One calm question at a time, never a scrollable form, while the household canvas grows beside it — 'the conversation does the input; THE CANVAS HOLDS THE CONTEXT.' On mobile the canvas collapses to a ribbon of faces with the running total pinned right. Independently corroborated by Savage's whole method ('ask, don't tell') — the corpus validating an instinct the design already had, which is exactly the corpus's sanctioned role.

nodes.label: Triage selects the insight (insight is rationed)
nodes.rationale: 'INSIGHT IS RATIONED, NOT DASHBOARDED. We have three strong revelations and SHOWING ALL THREE IS HOW THIS BECOMES OVERBEARING. Triage selects which one you get: retirement → THE SCP CLAWBACK · my family → THE CANVAS AND THE GAP · debt → THE LEAK. ONE JOURNEY, ONE HEADLINE.' The discipline that stops a research-rich engine from becoming an overwhelming interface — and the reason accumulating more domain findings does not degrade the UX.
nodes.norm_label: triage selects the insight (insight is rationed)

nodes.label: Depth in the engine, not the interface
nodes.rationale: THE TEST FOR ANY NEW DOMAIN DISCOVERY: 'DOES IT ADD A QUESTION, OR AN INSIGHT? IF IT ADDS A QUESTION, IT FAILED.' Everything the research surfaced — 16 NIS classes, four SCP cliffs, Health Surcharge, PAYE brackets, 70% deductibility, two needs methodologies, the benchmark — is DERIVED FROM THE SAME FIVE ANSWERS, not asked. The ONLY addition is 'when did you start working?' (NIS contribution weeks), 'which fits the conversation rather than a form.' This is the invariant that reconciles the project's enormous parameter depth with the five-question promise.
nodes.norm_label: depth in the engine, not the interface

nodes.label: Annuities are IN SCOPE
nodes.rationale: ✅ RESOLVED IN §4: 'ANNUITIES ARE IN SCOPE. In T&T, annuities fall under the LIFE LICENCE — a CBTT-registered life agent is licensed to sell them, and NO TTSEC REGISTRATION IS INVOLVED.' Source: the founder, a CBTT-registered agent of 13+ years. Consistent with Tatil's own disclaimer and with Round 2's finding that Securities Act 'investment advice' attaches to SECURITIES specifically. 'This SUPERSEDES the earlier deferral, WHICH WAS BASED ON MY INFERENCE RATHER THAN PRACTITIONER KNOWLEDGE.' CONSEQUENCE: retirement becomes FIRST-CLASS IN V1, not roadmap — it is Tatil's Need #1, the engine substantially exists in the repo, the SCP clawback is our strongest insight, and it is the founder's deepest expertise. §8 confirms: 'Annuities and the TT$60k envelope (#6) are IN.' Still out of v1: unit-linked / investment-linked products where an explicit securities component may attach — 'narrow, and revisit with counsel — DO NOT LET IT RE-BLOCK ANNUITIES.' ⚠️⚠️ INTERNAL CONTRADICTION IN THE SPEC — FLAGGED: §7's risk table still carries the row 'Investment-linked products straddle two regimes | Medium | DEFERRED FROM V1. LEGAL REVIEW BEFORE ADDING ANNUITIES/UL/ENDOWMENT.' That row names ANNUITIES as deferred pending legal review, directly contradicting §4's licence finding and §8's 'annuities are in'. §1's insight-1 caveat is the softer, consistent version ('investment-linked products (universal life, endowment, annuities) MAY STRADDLE both regimes — legal review required'). The §7 row appears to be un-updated residue of the superseded deferral; §4 is the later, practitioner-sourced position and should govern. RESOLVE BEFORE BUILD: §7 must be amended to scope the deferral to unit-linked/investment-linked products only, striking 'annuities' from the deferred list, or the spec asserts both that annuities are v1 scope and that they are not.

nodes.label: Banhelyi 125 Action Statements & Power Phrases
nodes.author: Carlos 'Chas' Banhelyi, CFP/ACIP
nodes.rationale: PERSUASION LITERATURE, NOT ENGINE RULES. 125 phrases collected over 35 years by an Australian financial adviser (CFP/ACIP, 30+ years) and shared freely for a 'win-win' outcome; circulated by the founder to Pan-American Life colleagues Jan 2015. Belongs at the AI edges ONLY: it informs HOW a recommendation is explained, never WHAT is recommended. The transferable asset is the rhetorical STRUCTURE, not the wording -- much of the wording is 1950s-80s vintage and used verbatim in T&T in 2026 would range from dated to actively wrong. The standing test: does it help explain a recommendation the engine already made on the merits, or is it doing the recommending? Only the first is allowed.

nodes.label: Rhetorical Structure (the transferable asset)
nodes.rationale: The document's central claim: the structures are timeless, the wording is not. Rule for the explanation layer: keep the structure, replace the cast. Six structures are enumerated.

nodes.label: Tag Question Device
nodes.rationale: '...isn't it? / ...aren't they? / ...don't they?' Roughly a third of the 125 phrases end this way. A deliberate device: it INVITES AGREEMENT RATHER THAN ASSERTING a claim, converting a statement into something the client completes themselves. Examples: #5 'More good things are lost by indecision than by wrong decision, aren't they?'; #33 'No debt should last longer than the person who created it, should it?'. Matches the fact-find tone -- 'it doesn't have to be official' is the same move: it invites rather than asserts.

nodes.label: Reversal Device
nodes.rationale: Flip the objection's subject from the client to the family. #3 'You can say I don't need it, but can you say my family won't need it?'; #16 reverses the face-amount objection onto the spouse. The structure survives de-gendering even where the original wording does not.

nodes.label: Reframe Device
nodes.rationale: Recast a cost as a choice already being made. #6 'Someone always pays for life insurance, whether a man buys or not; the question is, who -- the man or his family?'; #34 'If you buy insurance or not, in the end someone will pay for it.'

nodes.label: Analogy Device
nodes.rationale: Make the abstract physical. Explicitly named as Feldman's signature and THE STRONGEST DEVICE IN THE LIST. Instances: #14 spare tyre/umbrella/parachute; #41 'insure the eggs or the goose that laid them?'; #99 three-legged stool (death, early retirement, long-term disability); #115-116 the money machine; #60 'Life insurance is like a parachute... if you ever want it and have not got it, you will never need it again.' The goose/eggs, three-legged stool and money machine analogies are keepers -- they make the abstract concrete, which is exactly what the leak visual and the obligation counter already do.

nodes.label: Contrast Pair Device
nodes.rationale: Two states, one line. #9 'Wives may not believe in life insurance, but widows always do'; #8 'The difference between an old man and an elderly gentleman can be a decent income'; #22 'It isn't easy to be old or poor, but it's a great deal worse to be both.' Note #9 is simultaneously the canonical contrast pair AND a gendered-framing trap -- the structure survives, the gendering does not.

nodes.label: Cost-of-Inaction Device
nodes.rationale: Price the decision, not the product. #65 'Would you rather make an $800 mistake or a $250,000 mistake?'; #44 'A lot of people do nothing wrong; they just do nothing. That's what's wrong.' Distinct from the coercive phrases -- this frames a cost, it does not apply pressure.

nodes.label: Phrase #45 -- 'What formula did you use?'
nodes.rationale: 'What formula did you use to arrive at the amount of life insurance you have at the moment?' Called THE PERFECT POLICY X-RAY OPENER and possibly the single most useful line in the list for the wedge. Non-confrontational, and almost nobody can answer it. It creates the gap conversation WITHOUT ASSERTING ANYTHING -- then the ledger plus needs engine answer it for the client. Becomes a fact-find soft question: 'What formula did you use to arrive at the cover you have now?' It's honest: it doesn't assert a gap, it reveals one.

nodes.label: Phrase #125 -- the CLICO opener
nodes.rationale: 'What has been the major problem you have had with my industry in the past that I would need to be aware of as we build a relationship together?' Assessed as brilliant: it invites the objection BEFORE it becomes resistance, and in T&T the answer is almost always CLICO. Surfaces CLICO on the client's terms rather than as silent resistance. Pairs directly with the trust layer (idea #9) and AM Best's affirmation of Tatil. Explicitly rated BETTER THAN Tolani's #36 because it is an opener rather than a rebuttal.

nodes.label: Phrase #31 -- 'You may last longer than your money'
nodes.rationale: Maps onto the NIS retirement gap, and unlike most of the list this one is provable with facts already verified: whole-life averaging, the $13,600 insurable-earnings ceiling, the $3,000 minimum pension, the SCP offset, and the actuary's own GAP of 25.5%. The phrase supplies the register; the verified fact supplies the substance. NOTE: a different phrase also numbered #31 in the gendered cluster ('My wife does not need insurance as she is a housewife') appears in the source -- the numbering is AMBIGUOUS between the two sections.
nodes.norm_label: phrase #31 -- 'you may last longer than your money'

nodes.label: Phrase-to-Verified-Fact Mapping Table
nodes.rationale: Called 'the payoff'. These aren't persuasion -- they're openers for evidence the engine already holds. Mappings: #51 and #124 -> the $1,300/month usable-income leak; #55 -> Human Life Value / NeedsEngine; #94-95 (disability framing) -> GapCalculator and health-shock modeling; #91 -> PALIG net-worth method; #113 -> LifeSPAN CI plus the T&T 25% female benefit on breast/gynae cancer; #66/#83/#109 -> CI and mortgage protection; #96 ('modern medicine is converting death to disability') -> CI plus the Caribbean NCD burden (diabetes, hypertension, cardiac); #32 -> estate equalisation plus the household canvas.

nodes.label: Business-Market Phrase Cluster (#21, 27, 28, 47, 68, 110)
nodes.rationale: Buy/sell agreements, partnership succession, sole-proprietor reality checks. Points at the already-flagged business market gap: Cashbuilder III (s.134(6A) employer-owned), Corporate Destiny and Group products all exist, and the founder holds both licences. #21 'Any partnership that operates without a proper buy/sell agreement is living on borrowed time'; #47 the disabled-partner 100%-work-for-50%-profits question; #110 the sole-proprietor beach test.

nodes.label: TRAP: Estate/Tax Framings That Don't Exist in T&T
nodes.rationale: LOAD-BEARING FINDING. Why each is wrong for T&T: #37 (capital gains tax planning) -- T&T has NO capital gains tax on most assets. #58 ('would your executor be embarrassed by the lack of liquidity in your estate?') and the estate-liquidity theme generally -- T&T has NO estate, inheritance, or gift tax, so the entire US/Australian estate-liquidity pitch is inapplicable. #59 estate equalisation survives but for a DIFFERENT REASON: probate speed and asset titling, not tax -- life insurance proceeds bypass probate, and THAT is the T&T estate pitch. #106 'superannuation' is Australian; T&T is NIS + approved annuity. #123 dollar's future value is fine but weaker than T&T-specific inflation and the $3,000 NIS minimum unindexed since 2012. This is the same localization failure the whole project exists to avoid -- importing a US/AU planning assumption that doesn't hold here. The estate-tax driver was ALREADY STRIPPED from the NeedsEngine for exactly this reason.
nodes.norm_label: trap: estate/tax framings that don't exist in t&t

nodes.label: TRAP: Gendered Framing Contradicts the Household Model
nodes.rationale: THE MOST IMPORTANT TENSION IN THE DOCUMENT. A large fraction of the 125 assume male breadwinner / female homemaker / nuclear family: #2 'a home without a mother... a mother without a home'; #9 'Wives may not believe... widows always do'; #15/#61 'the worst time for a wife to become a breadwinner'; #31 'My wife does not need insurance as she is a housewife' (Tolani #31 too); #62 'One ordinary father can support four children'; #64 'If every wife knew what every widow knows...'. The household canvas EXPLICITLY REJECTS this -- it was designed for elderly parents, outside children, supported nephews, relatives overseas: 'it doesn't have to be official.' That was the whole point of idea #14 and it's the thing no US tool models. Using 'wives and widows' language would UNDERCUT THE SINGLE MOST DIFFERENTIATED DESIGN DECISION. Better register: #92 'your partner'; better still #73 'If you weren't here, who would you want to take care of your obligations?' -- obligor-neutral, and exactly what the canvas asks. RULE: keep the structure, replace the cast.
nodes.norm_label: trap: gendered framing contradicts the household model

nodes.label: TRAP: Coercive Phrases (#19, #24, #43) -- Excluded
nodes.rationale: #19 'You can put me off, but you can't put my competitors off -- death and disability'; #24 'Whatever reason you may have for not starting this plan now will only sound ridiculous to your widow'; #43 'Anybody who doesn't believe in it ought to have the right to die without it at least once.' These are PRESSURE, NOT INFORMATION. They sit badly against the Market Conduct Guideline's suitability duties and against a product whose entire pitch is 'we don't optimise for commission.' Verdict: EXCLUDE.

nodes.label: How This Enters the Product (edges only)
nodes.rationale: IT DOES NOT ENTER THE ENGINE. It enters the AIExplanationService and the fact-find's soft questions, as a REGISTER -- nothing more. Concretely: (1) #45 becomes a fact-find soft question and X-ray opener; (2) #125 becomes the trust opener that surfaces CLICO on the client's terms; (3) the analogies (#41 goose/eggs, #99 three-legged stool, #115 money machine) are keepers; (4) the tag-question device matches the fact-find tone; (5) everything gendered gets recast obligor-neutral, everything estate-tax gets deleted, everything coercive gets excluded. The test, unchanged: does it help explain a recommendation the engine already made on the merits -- or is it doing the recommending? Only the first is allowed.
nodes.norm_label: how this enters the product (edges only)

nodes.label: Mode A — ASSISTED (face-to-face)
nodes.source_location: §3.2b Mode A — ASSISTED (face-to-face) · BUILD THIS FIRST
nodes.rationale: BUILD FIRST. Agent and client at one screen, one table. This is the §5 design: conversation drives / canvas reflects, the dual-view obligation counter, presentation mode. The agent is present, so the agent is the interpreter in real time. Founder's quote: 'if we are in a meeting and we are one-on-one or face-to-face with the client, we can use the tool to conduct the fact-finding and help with some solutions.' Status: decision locked in the §2 table.

nodes.label: Mode B — UNASSISTED (client link)
nodes.source_location: §3.2b Mode B — UNASSISTED (client link) · THEN THIS
nodes.rationale: BUILD SECOND. A NAMED client sent a PERSONAL link — explicitly NOT an anonymous public calculator. They complete the SAME full fact-find on their own time and see 'the potential' (ideas, not a recommendation), with the agent watching from the back end. Founder: 'they could kind of do it on their own with us at the backend... but it will still be validated by a real agent. Even if they go through the whole process at 2:00 in the morning, a real insurance agent or financial advisor will vet what they entered and what the system came up with.' Mid-funnel, distinct from the top-of-funnel public calculators.

nodes.label: The Validation Gate
nodes.source_location: §3.2b 🔑 The Validation Gate — the architectural heart of both modes
nodes.rationale: THE ARCHITECTURAL HEART of both modes. The agent vets BOTH (a) what the client entered and (b) what the engine produced, before anything becomes a recommendation. Nothing the client sees unassisted is a recommendation — it is a projection of potential; the recommendation only exists once a registered agent has vetted it. This makes agent_recommender_of_record a mechanism rather than an aspiration. Regulatorily clean — the agent is the recommender under the Insurance Act; the software proposes, the agent disposes. Commercially right — 'we as the insurance agent can pick up from there to bring them to a close.' It is also the answer to the self-serve risk.

nodes.label: One fact-find, two modes
nodes.source_location: §3.2b 'What differs between the modes — and what must not'
nodes.rationale: DESIGN CORRECTION by the founder: this was earlier specced as a shallow public 'provocation calculator' separate from the deep agent fact-find. It is actually ONE full fact-find with two modes. 'Do not build two fact-finds. Build one, with a mode flag and an agent-presence assumption.' SAME across modes: the five questions, the household canvas, the needs engine, the gap, the parameter tables, the validation gate. DIFFERENT: who drives; whether interpretation is live or deferred; the obligation counter (dual-view + presentation mode in Mode A; in Mode B there is no agent to hide it from so the client simply sees the reveal); and the copy register (Mode A can be conversational because a human carries the tone, Mode B must be self-explanatory).

nodes.label: The self-serve risk — a wrong number is worse than no number
nodes.source_location: §3.2b 🔴 The self-serve risk — and why the gate is the real answer
nodes.rationale: A wrong self-serve number is WORSE than no number. A client with conviction built on a bad figure is harder to correct than one with no figure — you are arguing against their own arithmetic, which they trust more than yours. Stated identically in both the spec and parameters/README.md, which makes it the module's stated reason for existing. Not hypothetical: the stale 2008 NIS table in the public calculators is the live instance.
nodes.norm_label: the self-serve risk — a wrong number is worse than no number

nodes.label: Two defences: correct parameters + the human gate
nodes.rationale: Both are required. Defence 1 = correct parameters (/parameters implemented: one source of truth for engine AND calculators, every value carrying effective date, source, retrieval date and status; verify.mjs in CI for both repos). Defence 2 = the human gate ('it will still be validated by a real agent'). THE GATE IS THE MORE ROBUST DEFENCE: parameters can still drift, a client can still mis-enter, and the engine can still hit a case nobody modelled — the agent catches it before it becomes conviction. Defence 1 alone assumes we are never wrong; the gate assumes we sometimes are.
nodes.norm_label: two defences: correct parameters + the human gate

nodes.label: Copy rule: 'the potential', never 'your recommendation'
nodes.rationale: Copy rule for Mode B: the client sees 'here's the potential', NEVER 'here's your recommendation'. Surface every caveat from ParameterTables in the client UI too — when the engine says 'increments unconfirmed', the client's screen says so. An honest gap beats a confident wrong number, especially when the client owns the number. This is the copy-level expression of what the validation gate enforces architecturally.

nodes.label: The public calculators are a third, separate thing
nodes.rationale: The five public calculators are a THIRD, separate thing — anonymous, SEO'd, top-of-funnel. No named client, no link, NO GATE. nodes.label: Parameter status vocabulary
nodes.rationale: Ten statuses, each a claim about how far a value can be trusted: VERIFIED (confirmed from the issuing agency with source URL and date) · VERIFIED_SINGLE_SOURCE (only one source found) · VERIFIED_PRACTICE_UNCITED (real and safe to compute with, but no statutory basis located — do not claim a legal citation) · VERIFIED_MARKET_STANDARD (not law; market convention confirmed across independent insurers) · MARKET_CONVENTION (a local norm, not a universal truth — encode as a parameter, never a constant) · PROVISIONAL (announced but not gazetted; never show to a client as settled) · DERIVED (computed by us from verified inputs, not published directly) · BLOCKING_UNRESOLVED (ships nothing; must be answered before the dependent feature) · UNVERIFIED_1995_SOURCE (from a dated document; may not survive) · STALE_DO_NOT_USE (superseded; retained only so drift is detectable). assertSafe() throws on BLOCKING_UNRESOLVED, PROVISIONAL, UNVERIFIED_1995_SOURCE and STALE_DO_NOT_USE.

nodes.label: NIS benefit-rate drift (2008 → 2016) fixed
nodes.source_location: ## Why this is load-bearing, not hygiene
nodes.rationale: The live example the parameters module exists to fix. The public calculators held the STALE 2008 NIS benefit table (Class I 335.83); the current 2016 schedule is Class I 566.72 — understating the pension by 69%, which OVERSTATES the retirement gap, which SELLS MORE PRODUCT. That is the self-serving direction, and in a self-serve model it would be wearing THE CLIENT'S OWN AUTHORITY. Root cause is the per-page trust failure: NIBTT publishes benefit rates in two places with ~69% different values and never reconciles them — the Benefits section serves the stale 2008 table (and its own Retirement pages link to it) while the current 2016 table sits under /Contribution_Rates/. Status: drift identified and corrected in the module; the spec still carries it as BLOCKING against the engine's PENSION_RATES port.

nodes.label: Class Z Class-XVI typo corrected (220.72 → 20.72)
nodes.rationale: NIBTT prints 220.72 for Class XVI. Class Z is exactly 5.00% of the class weekly total for every class I–XV, so the Class XVI value must be 20.72 — a stray leading '2' in the issuer's own publication. Do not propagate NIBTT's typo. AMBIGUOUS as sourced: the derivation and correction are asserted in the task brief and consistent with the README's documented pattern of NIBTT self-contradiction, but the specific figures do not appear verbatim in either file read for this chunk — flagging rather than omitting.

nodes.label: Assisted-first sequencing
nodes.rationale: Founder's call, locked in the §2 decisions table: ASSISTED (face-to-face) first, UNASSISTED (client link) second. 'Build where the human is present, learn what the tool needs, then remove the human's presence once it's trusted.' Both modes share one fact-find and one validation gate (§3.2b). The sequencing is an epistemic argument, not a resourcing one — the assisted mode is how you find out what the unassisted mode has to carry alone.

nodes.label: Quotations / rating deferred
nodes.rationale: DEFERRED — learn the real process from the founder's portal first. Founder: 'What I will do in the future is show you how to do the real calculations in terms of quotations... how to use our actual written portal to run quotes.' The 192-quote rate grid seeds RateProvider for STRUCTURE, but DO NOT reverse-engineer the quoting process from it — that is the same inference error that misclassified Platinum Edge (specced as a permanent life product when it is an unapproved deferred annuity). The rule generalises: the artefact tells you the shape, the practitioner tells you the process.

nodes.label: NIS increments — BLOCKING_UNRESOLVED
nodes.rationale: Status BLOCKING. The 2016 schedule publishes BASICS ONLY, no increment column. 2008 = 4.90…46.76; 2013 = 6.11…56.33; 2016 = unpublished. Two readings exist, neither adopted. Must be confirmed with NIBTT or the Legal Notices (25–30) before the pension formula ships. Until then nisPension() DELIBERATELY REFUSES TO GUESS — it returns the basic + minimum and surfaces a caveat instead. The formula structure is confirmed; the current increment values are not. This is the design pattern the whole module encodes: an honest gap beats a confident wrong number.
